translations.idiomatic: Fu Zonglong and Wang Qiaonian

translations.idiomatic: (Zhang Guoqin and others)〉

translations.idiomatic: Yang Wenyue

translations.literal: (Fu Ruwei and others)〉

translations.literal: Sun Chuanting
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuanting

sentences.zh: 傅宗龍，字仲綸，昆明人。

translations.literal: Fu Zonglong, styled Zhonglun, was a man of Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zonglong, whose courtesy name was Zhonglun, came from Kunming.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除銅梁知縣，調巴縣，行取，入為戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Tongliang, transferred to Ba County, then selected for capital office and entered as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as magistrate of Tongliang and then Ba County, he was selected for promotion to the capital and appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 久之，授御史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was made a censor.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，遼陽破，帝下募兵之令，宗龍請行。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, Liaoyang fell, the emperor issued an order to recruit troops, and Zonglong volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi, after Liaoyang fell, the emperor called for recruits; Zonglong offered to undertake the mission himself.

sentences.zh: 一月余，得精卒五千。

translations.literal: In a little over a month he obtained five thousand elite soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Within little more than a month he had raised five thousand crack troops.

sentences.zh: 明年，安邦彥反，圍貴陽，土寇蜂起。

translations.literal: The next year An Bangyan rebelled, besieged Guiyang, and native bandits rose everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The following year An Bangyan rebelled and laid siege to Guiyang, while native raiders swarmed across the region.

sentences.zh: 請發帑金濟滇將士，開建昌，通由蜀入滇之路，別設偏沅巡撫，罷湖廣退怯總兵薛來允。

translations.literal: He requested disbursement of treasury funds to aid Yunnan troops, opening Jianchang to clear the route from Shu into Yunnan, establishing a separate Pian-Yuan grand coordinator, and dismissing the cowardly Huguang regional commander Xue Laiyun.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the court to release treasury silver for Yunnan's armies, reopen Jianchang to restore the Sichuan route into Yunnan, create a separate Pian-Yuan grand coordinator, and remove the timid Huguang regional commander Xue Laiyun.

sentences.zh: 帝多采納之。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted most of these proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted most of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 又上疏自請討賊，言：「為武定、尋甸患者，東川土酋祿千鐘。

translations.literal: He again memorialized, volunteering to suppress the rebels, saying: "The trouble for Wuding and Xundian is the Dongchuan native chieftain Lu Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial offering to lead the campaign himself, writing: "The scourge of Wuding and Xundian is the Dongchuan chieftain Lu Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 為沾益、羅平患者，賊婦設科及其黨李賢輩。

translations.literal: The trouble for Zhanyi and Luoping is the rebel woman She Ke and her faction Li Xian and others.
translations.idiomatic: The scourge of Zhanyi and Luoping is the rebel woman She Ke and her followers, including Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 攻圍普安，為滇、黔門戶患者，龍文治妻及其黨尹二。

translations.literal: Those besieging Pu'an, the gateway of Yunnan and Guizhou, are the wife of Long Wenzhi and her faction Yin Er.
translations.idiomatic: Those threatening Pu'an—the gateway between Yunnan and Guizhou—are the wife of Long Wenzhi and her lieutenant Yin Er.

sentences.zh: 困安南，據關索嶺者，沙國珍及羅應魁輩。

translations.literal: Those harassing Annan and holding Guansuoling are Sha Guozhen and Luo Yingkui and their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Those harrying Annan and holding Guansuoling Pass are Sha Guozhen, Luo Yingkui, and their bands.

sentences.zh: 困烏撒者，安效良。

translations.literal: The one troubling Wusa is An Xiaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: The man plaguing Wusa is An Xiaoliang.

sentences.zh: 臣皆悉其生平，非臣敵。

translations.literal: Your servant knows all their careers; none are a match for your servant.
translations.idiomatic: I know each of them well—they are no match for me.

sentences.zh: 臣願以四川巡按兼貴州監軍，滅此群醜。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes, as Sichuan touring censor concurrently supervising Guizhou forces, to destroy this pack of villains.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to serve as Sichuan touring censor with concurrent command over Guizhou troops, and to wipe out this whole rabble.

sentences.zh: 」帝大喜，下所司議。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased and referred the matter to the relevant offices for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted and ordered the ministries to consider the plan.

sentences.zh: 會宗龍以疾歸，不果行。

translations.literal: Just then Zonglong returned home on account of illness, and the mission did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: But Zonglong fell ill and went home before he could set out.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，貴州巡撫王三善為降賊陳其愚所紿，敗歿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Guizhou grand coordinator Wang Shanshan was deceived by the surrendered rebel Chen Qiyu and died in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, Guizhou grand coordinator Wang Shanshan was lured into a trap by the surrendered rebel Chen Qiyu and killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 其夏即家起宗龍巡按其地，兼監軍。

translations.literal: That summer, from his home, Zonglong was raised to tour and inspect that region, concurrently supervising the army.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the court recalled Zonglong from retirement to tour the region and supervise military affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，部檄滇撫閔洪學援黔，以不能過盤江而止。

translations.literal: Earlier the ministry had ordered Yunnan grand coordinator Min Hongxue to aid Guizhou, but he stopped because he could not cross the Pan River.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the ministry had ordered Yunnan grand coordinator Min Hongxue to relieve Guizhou, but his force halted at the Pan River, unable to cross.

sentences.zh: 宗龍既被命，洪學令參政謝存仁、參將袁善及土官普名聲、沙如玉等以兵五千送之。

translations.literal: Once Zonglong received his commission, Hongxue ordered administrative commissioner Xie Cunren, deputy commander Yuan Shan, and native officials Pu Mingsheng, Sha Ruyu, and others to escort him with five thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Zonglong received his orders, Hongxue sent administrative commissioner Xie Cunren, deputy commander Yuan Shan, and native leaders Pu Mingsheng and Sha Ruyu with five thousand men to escort him.

sentences.zh: 宗龍直渡盤江，戰且行，寇悉破。

translations.literal: Zonglong crossed the Pan River directly, fighting as he advanced, and broke all the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong crossed the Pan River at once, fighting his way forward and shattering every enemy force in his path.

sentences.zh: 乃謝遣存仁、善，以名聲等土兵七百人入貴陽，擒斬其愚，軍民大快。

translations.literal: He then dismissed Cunren and Shan with thanks, entered Guiyang with seven hundred native troops under Mingsheng and others, captured and executed Qiyu, and soldiers and civilians rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Cunren and Shan back with thanks, entered Guiyang with seven hundred native troops under Mingsheng, captured and executed Qiyu, and the army and populace celebrated.

sentences.zh: 宗龍盡知黔中要害及土酋逆順，將士勇怯。

translations.literal: Zonglong knew thoroughly the strategic points of Guizhou and which native chiefs were loyal or rebellious, and which officers and soldiers were brave or timid.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong had mastered every strategic point in Guizhou, knew which chieftains would stand or turn, and could read the courage or cowardice of every officer and soldier.

sentences.zh: 巡撫蔡復一倚信之，請敕宗龍專理軍務，設中軍旗鼓，裨將以下聽賞罰，可之。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Cai Fuyi relied on him and requested an imperial order that Zonglong alone manage military affairs, establish a central army staff with banners and drums, and that officers below deputy commander obey his rewards and punishments; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Cai Fuyi came to rely on him entirely and asked the throne to put Zonglong in sole charge of operations, with his own headquarters staff and authority to reward or punish any officer below deputy commander rank; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 宗龍乃條上方略，又備陳黔中艱苦，請大發餉金，亦報可。

translations.literal: Zonglong then submitted a detailed strategic plan, also fully describing the hardships of Guizhou and requesting a large disbursement of pay funds; this too was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong laid out his strategy in full, described the grinding hardships of the Guizhou campaign, and asked for a major release of funds—all of which was approved.

sentences.zh: 初，三善令監軍道臣節制諸將，文武不和，進退牽制。

translations.literal: Earlier Shanshan had ordered the army-supervising circuit official to control the generals; civil and military did not cooperate, and advance and retreat were mutually constrained.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Shanshan, the army-supervising circuit official had held command over the generals, leaving civil and military at odds and every movement hamstrung.

sentences.zh: 宗龍反其所為，令監軍給芻糧，核功罪，不得專進止。

translations.literal: Zonglong reversed this practice, ordering the supervisor to supply fodder and grain, verify merit and fault, and forbidding exclusive control over advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong reversed the arrangement: the supervisor would supply provisions and assess merit and fault, but would no longer control movements.

sentences.zh: 由是諸將用命，連破賊汪家沖、蔣義寨，直抵織金。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals obeyed orders, successively breaking the rebel strongholds Wangjiachong and Jiangyizhai and pushing straight to Zhijin.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the generals fought with full commitment, storming Wangjiachong and Jiangyizhai in succession and driving all the way to Zhijin.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，總理魯欽敗績於陸廣河。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, supreme commander Lu Qin suffered defeat at the Luguang River.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, supreme commander Lu Qin was routed on the Luguang River.

sentences.zh: 宗龍上言：「不合滇、蜀，則黔不能平賊；

translations.literal: Zonglong memorialized: "Without combining Yunnan and Shu, Guizhou cannot pacify the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong wrote: "Without coordinating Yunnan and Sichuan, Guizhou cannot crush the rebels;

sentences.zh: 不專總督任，則不能合滇、蜀兵。

translations.literal: without concentrating the governor-general's authority, one cannot combine the armies of Yunnan and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: and without a governor-general with full authority, those two armies cannot be brought together."

sentences.zh: 請召還朱燮元，以復一兼督四川，開府遵義，而移蜀撫駐永寧，滇撫駐沾益，黔撫駐陸廣，沅撫駐偏橋，四面並進，發餉二百萬金給之。

translations.literal: He requested recall of Zhu Xieyuan, that Fuyi concurrently supervise Sichuan and establish headquarters at Zunyi, while moving the Shu grand coordinator to Yongning, the Yunnan coordinator to Zhanyi, the Guizhou coordinator to Luguang, the Yuan coordinator to Pianqiao, advancing on four sides together, and disbursing two million taels of pay.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Zhu Xieyuan be recalled, that Fuyi also take Sichuan and open headquarters at Zunyi, that the Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, and Yuan coordinators each move to Yongning, Zhanyi, Luguang, and Pianqiao respectively, that all four fronts advance together, and that two million taels be allocated for pay.

sentences.zh: 更設黔、蜀巡撫。

translations.literal: He also proposed establishing separate Guizhou and Shu grand coordinators.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed new Guizhou and Sichuan grand coordinators.

sentences.zh: 」帝以復一新敗，令解官，即以燮元代，而命尹同臯撫蜀，王瑊撫黔，沅撫閔夢得移鎮，一如宗龍議。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because Fuyi had just been defeated, ordered him dismissed and replaced him with Xieyuan, appointing Yin Tonggao to govern Shu, Wang Ji to govern Guizhou, and Yuan coordinator Min Mengde to transfer his post—all exactly as Zonglong had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " Because Fuyi had just suffered defeat, the emperor removed him and installed Xieyuan in his place, appointing Yin Tonggao to Sichuan, Wang Ji to Guizhou, and moving Yuan coordinator Min Mengde—all exactly as Zonglong had urged.

sentences.zh: 陸廣敗後，諸苗復蠢動。

translations.literal: After the Luguang defeat, the various Miao stirred again.
translations.idiomatic: After the disaster at Luguang, the Miao tribes rose again across the region.

sentences.zh: 復一、宗龍謀，討破烏粟、螺螄、長田諸叛苗，大破平越賊，毀其砦百七十，賊黨漸孤。

translations.literal: Fuyi and Zonglong planned together, suppressed the rebellious Miao at Wusu, Luosi, and Changtian, inflicted a great defeat on the Pingyue rebels, destroyed one hundred seventy of their stockades, and the rebel factions grew increasingly isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyi and Zonglong planned a joint campaign, crushed the rebel Miao at Wusu, Luosi, and Changtian, routed the Pingyue rebels and destroyed one hundred seventy of their stockades, leaving the rebel bands increasingly isolated.

sentences.zh: 宗龍乃條上屯守策，言：

translations.literal: Zonglong then submitted in detail a garrison-and-colonization plan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong then laid out his garrison-and-settlement strategy in full:

sentences.zh: 蜀以屯為守，黔則當以守為屯。

translations.literal: Shu uses colonization as defense; Guizhou should use defense as colonization.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan defends by colonizing the frontier; Guizhou must colonize by defending it.

sentences.zh: 蓋安酋土地半在水外，仡佬、龍仲、蔡苗諸雜種，緩急與相助。

translations.literal: For the An chieftains' lands are half beyond the rivers, and the Gelao, Longzhong, Caimiao, and other mixed peoples aid one another in urgency or ease.
translations.idiomatic: The An chieftains hold land mostly south of the rivers, and the Gelao, Longzhong, Caimiao, and other tribes rally to one another as needed.

sentences.zh: 賊有外藩，我無邊蔽，黔兵所以分力愈詘。

translations.literal: The rebels have outer bulwarks while we lack frontier screens; this is why Guizhou troops are ever more divided and weakened.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels enjoy outer buffers while we have no frontier shield—hence Guizhou's forces are spread thin and grow weaker by the day.

sentences.zh: 臣謂以守為屯者，先發兵據河，奪賊所恃。

translations.literal: Your servant says that to use defense as colonization, one must first send troops to hold the rivers and seize what the rebels rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: To defend by settling, I propose first seizing the river crossings and stripping the rebels of their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 然後撫剿諸種，隨渡口大小，置大小寨，深溝高壘，置烽墩炮臺。

translations.literal: Then pacify and suppress the various peoples, and according to the size of each crossing establish large or small stockades with deep ditches and high ramparts, beacon towers, and gun platforms.
translations.idiomatic: Then pacify or subdue the tribes, and at every ford, large or small, build stockades with deep trenches, high walls, beacon towers, and gun emplacements.

sentences.zh: 小渡則塞以木石，使一粟不入水內，一賊不出水外，賊無如我何。

translations.literal: At small crossings block with timber and stone, so that not one grain enters the riverlands and not one rebel comes out beyond the water; then the rebels can do nothing against us.
translations.idiomatic: Block the minor crossings with timber and stone so that not a grain of grain crosses inward and not a rebel slips outward—and the enemy will be helpless against us.

sentences.zh: 又令沿河兵習水戰，當賊耕耨時，頻出奇兵，渡河擾之。

translations.literal: Also order the riverine troops to practice naval warfare, and when the rebels are planting and hoeing, frequently send raiding parties across the river to harass them.
translations.idiomatic: Train the river garrisons in water fighting, and during planting season send raiding parties across the river again and again to harry the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊不敢附河而居，而後我可以議屯也。

translations.literal: The rebels will not dare dwell along the rivers, and only then can we discuss colonization.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels dare not live along the rivers, we can begin to establish colonies in earnest.

sentences.zh: 屯之策有二：一曰清衛所原田，一曰割逆賊故壤，而以衛所之法行之。

translations.literal: The colonization strategy has two parts: first, clear the original fields of the guard posts; second, carve out the former territory of the rebel chieftains and apply the guard-post system to it.
translations.idiomatic: Settlement policy has two parts: reclaim the guard-post lands that have fallen idle, and carve up the rebels' former territory under the guard-post system.

sentences.zh: 蓋黔不患無田，患無人。

translations.literal: For Guizhou does not lack fields but lacks people.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou does not lack land—it lacks settlers.

sentences.zh: 客兵聚散無常，不能久駐，莫若仿祖制，盡舉屯田以授有功，因功大小，為官高下，自指揮至總、小旗，畀以應得田為世業，而禁其私賣買。

translations.literal: Mercenary troops assemble and disperse without constancy and cannot garrison long; better to follow the ancestral system, grant all colonized fields to those with merit, and according to the size of merit assign ranks from commander down to company and squad leaders, conferring the corresponding fields as hereditary estates while forbidding private sale.
translations.idiomatic: Mercenary troops come and go and cannot hold the frontier; better to follow the founding system and grant garrison lands to men of merit—commanders, company officers, and squad leaders alike—giving each his allotted fields as a hereditary estate and forbidding private sale.

sentences.zh: 不待招徠，戶口自實。

translations.literal: Without waiting for recruitment, households will fill in of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting to recruit settlers, the population will fill in on its own.

sentences.zh: 臣所謂以守為屯者如此。

translations.literal: Such is what your servant means by using defense as colonization.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I mean by defending through settlement.

sentences.zh: 然兵當用四萬八千人，餉當歲八十余萬，時當閱三年，如此而後賊可盡滅也。

translations.literal: Yet troops should number forty-eight thousand, annual pay should exceed eight hundred thousand, and time should span three years—only then can the rebels be utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: It will take forty-eight thousand troops, more than eight hundred thousand taels a year in pay, and three years of effort—only then can the rebels be wiped out completely.

sentences.zh: 部議從之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 復一卒，王瑊代，事悉倚辦。

translations.literal: Fuyi died and Wang Ji replaced him; all affairs were entrusted to Zonglong to manage.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuyi died, Wang Ji succeeded him, and Zonglong was left to handle everything.

sentences.zh: 宗龍乃漸剪水外逆黨，將大興屯田。

translations.literal: Zonglong then gradually cut down the rebel factions beyond the rivers and was about to launch colonization on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong steadily cut down the rebel bands south of the rivers and prepared to launch a major colonization drive.

sentences.zh: 邦彥懼，謀沮之，六年三月，大舉渡河入寇。

translations.literal: Bangyan feared this and plotted to thwart it; in the third month of the sixth year he crossed the river in force to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan, alarmed, plotted to stop him; in the third month of the sixth year he crossed the river in force to attack.

sentences.zh: 宗龍擊破邦彥趙官屯，斬老蟲添，威名大著。

translations.literal: Zonglong struck and broke Bangyan at Zhao'guantun, beheaded Lao Chongtian, and his renown grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong routed Bangyan at Zhao'guantun, killed Lao Chongtian, and his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 當是時，大帥新亡，全黔震動，燮元遠在蜀，瑊擁虛位，非宗龍，黔幾殆。

translations.literal: At that time the supreme commander had just died, all Guizhou was shaken, Xieyuan was far away in Shu, Ji held an empty title—without Zonglong, Guizhou would nearly have perished.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander had just fallen, all Guizhou was in turmoil, Xieyuan was far off in Sichuan, and Ji held only a nominal post—without Zonglong, Guizhou would have been lost.

sentences.zh: 詔加太仆少卿。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The court promoted him to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He then went home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年起故官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 用孫承宗薦，擢右僉都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: On Sun Chengzong's recommendation he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: On Sun Chengzong's recommendation he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜兵部右侍郎兼僉都御史，總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed vice minister of war, concurrently vice censor-in-chief, and governor-general of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made vice minister of war with concurrent rank as vice censor-in-chief and charged as governor-general of Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 用小故奪官矣。

translations.literal: On a minor pretext his office was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office over a minor matter.

sentences.zh: 居久之，十年十月流寇大入蜀，陷蜀三十余州縣，帝拊髀而思宗龍曰：「使宗龍撫蜀，賊安至是哉！

translations.literal: After he had dwelt at home a long time, in the tenth month of the tenth year the roving bandits entered Shu in force, capturing more than thirty prefectures and counties; the emperor slapped his thigh and thought of Zonglong, saying: "Had Zonglong governed Shu, how could the bandits have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval at home, in the tenth month of the tenth year roving rebels poured into Sichuan and overran more than thirty prefectures and counties. The emperor struck his thigh and said of Zonglong: "If Zonglong had been governing Sichuan, how could the rebels have reached this point!"

sentences.zh: 」趣即家起宗龍。

translations.literal: " He urgently raised Zonglong from his home.
translations.idiomatic: " He urgently recalled Zonglong from retirement.

sentences.zh: 宗龍至蜀，代王維章與總兵羅尚文禦卻賊。

translations.literal: Zonglong reached Shu, replaced Wang Weizhang, and with regional commander Luo Shangwen repelled the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong reached Sichuan, replaced Wang Weizhang, and with regional commander Luo Shangwen drove the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月，以楊嗣昌薦，召為兵部尚書，去蜀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twelfth year, on Yang Sichang's recommendation, he was summoned as minister of war and left Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twelfth year, on Yang Sichang's recommendation, he was summoned to the capital as minister of war and left Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 宗龍自定黔亂後，凡十有四年，輒起用，用不久輒遷去。

translations.literal: From the time Zonglong pacified the Guizhou rebellion, for fourteen years in all he was repeatedly raised to office, and whenever employed was soon transferred away.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he pacified Guizhou, over fourteen years he was repeatedly called back to service—and each time, before long, moved on again.

sentences.zh: 八月至京，入見帝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he reached the capital and had an audience with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the capital in the eighth month and was received in audience.

sentences.zh: 宗龍為人伉直任氣，不能從諛承意。

translations.literal: Zonglong was by nature upright and headstrong, unable to follow flattery and accommodate others' wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong was blunt and proud by nature, incapable of flattery or bending to another's will.

sentences.zh: 帝憤中樞失職，嗣昌以權詭得主知。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that the central command had failed in its duties; Sichang by crafty use of power won the ruler's favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious at the failures of the central command, while Sichang had won favor through cunning manipulation of power.

sentences.zh: 宗龍樸忠，初入見，即言民窮財盡。

translations.literal: Zonglong was plain and loyal; on his first audience he immediately spoke of the people's exhaustion and the treasury's depletion.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong was honest and plainspoken; at his first audience he declared outright that the people were exhausted and the treasury empty.

sentences.zh: 帝頗然之，顧豤言不已，遂怫然曰：「卿當整理兵事爾。

translations.literal: The emperor was somewhat persuaded, but as crude talk continued without end he grew displeased and said: "You should simply put military affairs in order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was partly persuaded, but as the blunt talk went on he grew annoyed and said: "Your job is to put the army in order.

sentences.zh: 」既退，語嗣昌曰：「何哉？

translations.literal: " After he withdrew, he said to Sichang: "What is this?
translations.idiomatic: " After Zonglong left, the emperor said to Sichang: "What was that?

sentences.zh: 宗龍善策黔，而所言卑卑，皆他人唾余，何也？

translations.literal: Zonglong is skilled at planning for Guizhou, yet what he said was petty—all leftovers others have spat out—why?
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong is a master of Guizhou strategy, yet everything he said was trite—leftovers everyone has chewed over already. Why?

sentences.zh: 」自是所奏請，多中格。

translations.literal: " From then on most of what he submitted was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on most of his proposals were turned down.

sentences.zh: 熊文粲既罷，宗龍乃言：「向者賊流突東西，嗣昌故建分剿之策。

translations.literal: After Xiong Wencan was dismissed, Zonglong said: "Formerly the bandits flowed east and west in sudden raids, so Sichang established the strategy of divided suppression.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiong Wencan was removed, Zonglong argued: "When the rebels were roaming east and west at will, Sichang devised the strategy of dividing forces to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 今則流突者各止其所，臣請收勢險節短之效。

translations.literal: Now those who flowed and raided have each stopped in place; your servant requests to gather the effect of holding strong positions and shortening the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Now each band has settled in one place; I propose we exploit terrain and fight short, decisive campaigns.

sentences.zh: 總理止轄楚、豫，秦督兼轄四川，鳳督兼轄安慶，各率所轄撫鎮，期十二月成功。

translations.literal: The supreme commander should govern only Chu and Yu; the Shaanxi governor should also govern Sichuan; the Fengyang governor should also govern Anqing; each should lead his grand coordinators and regional commanders and fix success within twelve months.
translations.idiomatic: Let the supreme commander hold only Huguang and Henan; let the Shaanxi governor also take Sichuan; let the Fengyang governor also take Anqing—each leading his coordinators and commanders to finish the campaign within twelve months.

sentences.zh: 」因薦湖廣巡撫方孔炤堪代文燦。

translations.literal: " He therefore recommended Huguang grand coordinator Fang Kongzhao as fit to replace Wencan.
translations.idiomatic: " He recommended Huguang grand coordinator Fang Kongzhao to replace Wencan.

sentences.zh: 帝不用，用嗣昌督師。

translations.literal: The emperor did not adopt this and instead used Sichang as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declined and appointed Sichang supreme commander instead.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌既督師，上章請兵食，不悉應，劾中樞不任。

translations.literal: Once Sichang became supreme commander, he memorialized requesting troops and provisions; not all was granted, and he impeached the central command as incompetent.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sichang took command, he asked for troops and supplies; the court did not fully comply, and he accused the central command of incompetence.

sentences.zh: 宗龍亦劾嗣昌徒耗敝國家，不能報效，以氣淩廷臣。

translations.literal: Zonglong also impeached Sichang for merely exhausting and impoverishing the state without repaying service, and for overbearing court officials with his arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong in turn accused Sichang of draining the treasury without results and bullying his colleagues at court.

sentences.zh: 會薊遼總督洪承疇請用劉肇基為團練總兵官，中官高起潛又揭肇基恇怯，宗龍不即覆。

translations.literal: Just then Ji-Liaodong governor-general Hong Chengchou requested Liu Zhaoji as training regional commander; eunuch Gao Qiqian also exposed Zhaoji as cowardly, and Zonglong did not reply promptly.
translations.idiomatic: About then Ji-Liaodong governor-general Hong Chengchou nominated Liu Zhaoji as training regional commander; eunuch Gao Qiqian denounced Zhaoji as timid, and Zonglong failed to respond promptly.

sentences.zh: 帝遂發怒，責以抗旨，令對狀。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew angry, rebuked him for defying the imperial will, and ordered him to answer charges at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, accused him of defying orders, and ordered him to answer the charges in person.

sentences.zh: 奏上，復以戲視封疆下吏。

translations.literal: When his memorial was submitted, he was again charged with treating frontier subordinates as a jest.
translations.idiomatic: When his reply was submitted, he was charged again with treating frontier officials as a joke.

sentences.zh: 法司擬戍邊，不許，欲置之死。

translations.literal: The judicial offices proposed banishment to the frontier; this was not permitted, and they wished to put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices recommended exile; the emperor refused and sought his death.

sentences.zh: 在獄二年矣，十四年春，嗣昌死，尚書陳新甲薦其才，帝未有以應也，良久曰：「樸忠，吾以夙負用之，宜盡死力。

translations.literal: He had been in prison two years when, in the spring of the fourteenth year, Sichang died; Minister Chen Xinjia recommended his talent, and the emperor had no immediate reply; after a long while he said: "Plain and loyal—I employ him for old obligations; he should exert himself unto death.
translations.idiomatic: He had been in prison two years when, in the spring of the fourteenth year, Sichang died. Minister Chen Xinjia recommended him, and after a long silence the emperor said: "He is honest and loyal—I owe him an old debt. He should give his life for the cause.

sentences.zh: 」遂釋之出獄，以兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史代丁啟睿，總督陜西三邊軍務。

translations.literal: " He then released him from prison, appointed him vice minister of war concurrently right vice censor-in-chief in place of Ding Qirui, and made him governor-general of the three frontiers of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: " He released him, appointed him vice minister of war with concurrent rank as right vice censor-in-chief in place of Ding Qirui, and made him governor-general of the Shaanxi frontiers.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，李自成有眾五十萬，自陷河、洛，犯開封，羅汝才復自南陽趨鄧、淅，與合兵。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng had a host of five hundred thousand; having himself seized the He and Luo regions, he attacked Kaifeng, while Luo Rucai again advanced from Nanyang toward Deng and Xi to join forces.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zicheng commanded five hundred thousand men, had overrun the Yellow and Luo river country, and was besieging Kaifeng, while Luo Rucai marched from Nanyang toward Dengzhou and Xixia to unite with him.

sentences.zh: 帝命宗龍專辦自成。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zonglong to deal exclusively with Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zonglong to concentrate solely on Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 議盡括關中兵餉以出，然屬郡旱蝗，已不能應。

translations.literal: It was proposed to levy all Guanzhong military pay and provisions for the campaign, but the subordinate prefectures suffered drought and locusts and could not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was to strip Guanzhong of every soldier and ration for the expedition, but drought and locusts had already left the surrounding prefectures unable to comply.

sentences.zh: 九月四日，以川、陜兵二萬出關，次新蔡，與保督楊文嶽兵會。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the ninth month he led twenty thousand Sichuan and Shaanxi troops out of the pass, halted at Xincai, and joined forces with Baoding grand coordinator Yang Wenyue.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the ninth month he marched twenty thousand Sichuan and Shaanxi troops through the pass, stopped at Xincai, and united with the army of Baoding grand coordinator Yang Wenyue.

sentences.zh: 賀人龍、李國奇將秦兵，虎大威將保兵，共結浮橋，東渡汝，合兵趨項城。

translations.literal: He Renlong and Li Guoqi commanded the Shaanxi troops, Hu Dawei commanded the Baoding troops; together they built a pontoon bridge, crossed the Ru River eastward, united their forces, and advanced on Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He Renlong and Li Guoqi led the Shaanxi force, Hu Dawei the Baoding force; together they threw a pontoon bridge across the Ru, crossed to the east bank, and marched on Xiangcheng as one army.

sentences.zh: 五日，兩軍畢渡，走龍口。

translations.literal: On the fifth day both armies finished crossing and hurried to Longkou.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day both armies finished crossing and pushed on to Longkou.

sentences.zh: 自成、汝才亦結浮橋於上流，將趨汝寧。

translations.literal: Zicheng and Rucai also built a pontoon bridge upstream and were about to advance on Runing.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng and Rucai had also built a pontoon bridge upstream and were preparing to march on Runing.

sentences.zh: 覘兩督兵至，盡伏精銳於林中，陽驅諸賊自浮橋西渡。

translations.literal: Seeing both governors' armies arrive, they hid all their elite troops in the woods and openly drove the rest of the bandits to cross westward over the pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When they saw both governors' armies arrive, they hid their crack troops in the woods and openly drove the rest of their men west across the pontoon bridge as a feint.

sentences.zh: 人龍使後騎覘賊，還報曰：「賊向汝矣，結浮橋將渡矣。

translations.literal: Renlong sent rear scouts to observe the bandits; they returned and reported: "The bandits are heading for the Ru and are building a pontoon bridge to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong sent scouts to the rear to watch the rebels; they came back reporting: "The rebels are heading for the Ru and building a pontoon bridge to cross."

sentences.zh: 」宗龍、文嶽夜會諸將於龍口，詰朝將戰。

translations.literal: " Zonglong and Wenyue met the generals at Longkou that night; they would fight at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: " That night Zonglong and Wenyue assembled the generals at Longkou and set battle for the next morning.

sentences.zh: 六日，兩軍並進，中道一騎馳而告曰：「賊畢渡矣。

translations.literal: On the sixth day both armies advanced together; midway a rider galloped up and reported: "The bandits have all crossed.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day both armies advanced together; midway a rider galloped up shouting: "The rebels have finished crossing!"

sentences.zh: 」復進，一騎馳而告曰：「賊半渡矣，三分渡其二矣。

translations.literal: " They advanced again; a rider galloped up and reported: "Half the bandits have crossed; two-thirds of the half have crossed.
translations.idiomatic: " They pushed on again; another rider galloped up: "Half the rebels have crossed—two-thirds of them are already over!"

sentences.zh: 」宗龍、文嶽曰：「驅之。

translations.literal: " Zonglong and Wenyue said: "Drive them.
translations.idiomatic: " Zonglong and Wenyue cried: "After them!"

sentences.zh: 」走三十里，至於孟家莊，日卓午。

translations.literal: " They raced thirty li to Mengjiazhuang; the sun stood at noon.
translations.idiomatic: " They raced thirty li to Mengjiazhuang, reaching it at high noon.

sentences.zh: 人龍、大威曰：「馬力乏矣，詰朝而戰，止兵為營。

translations.literal: Renlong and Dawei said: "The horses are exhausted; let us fight at dawn and halt the troops to make camp.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong and Dawei said: "The horses are spent—we should fight at dawn. Halt and make camp."

sentences.zh: 」諸軍弛馬甲，植戈錞，散行墟落求芻牧。

translations.literal: " The armies loosened armor from their horses, planted spears and halberds, and scattered through the hamlets seeking fodder and pasture.
translations.idiomatic: " The troops stripped their horses of armor, planted spears and halberds, and scattered through the villages looking for fodder.

sentences.zh: 賊覘之，塵起於林中，伏甲並出搏我兵。

translations.literal: The bandits observed this; dust rose from the woods and hidden armored troops all burst out to grapple with our soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels watched; dust rose from the woods and armored troops hidden there burst out and fell on the Ming army.

sentences.zh: 人龍有馬千騎不戰，國奇以麾下兵迎擊之，不勝。

translations.literal: Renlong had a thousand cavalry but would not fight; Guoqi met the attack with his own troops and could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong held a thousand cavalry in reserve and would not engage; Guoqi met the attack with his own men and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 秦兵、保兵俱潰，人龍、大威奔沈丘，國奇從之，三帥師潰。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi and Baoding troops both collapsed; Renlong and Dawei fled to Shenqiu, Guoqi followed, and the three commanders' armies were routed.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi and Baoding forces both broke; Renlong and Dawei fled to Shenqiu, Guoqi with them, and all three commanders' armies were routed.

sentences.zh: 宗龍、文嶽合兵屯火燒店，賊以步兵攻其營。

translations.literal: Zonglong and Wenyue united their troops and encamped at Huoshaodian; the bandits attacked the camp with infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong and Wenyue combined what remained and encamped at Huoshaodian; the rebels assaulted the camp with infantry.

sentences.zh: 諸軍鳴大炮，震死賊百余。

translations.literal: The armies fired great cannon and killed more than a hundred bandits by the blast.
translations.idiomatic: The army fired great guns and killed more than a hundred rebels with the blast.

sentences.zh: 日暮，賊引去。

translations.literal: At dusk the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宗龍軍西北，文嶽軍東南，畫塹而守。

translations.literal: Zonglong's army was to the northwest, Wenyue's to the southeast; they dug trenches and held.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong's force held the northwest, Wenyue's the southeast; they dug trenches and dug in.

sentences.zh: 保兵宵潰，保督副將挾文嶽騎而馳，夜奔於項城。

translations.literal: The Baoding troops collapsed by night; a deputy of the Baoding governor seized Wenyue on horseback and galloped away, fleeing to Xiangcheng by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Baoding troops broke that night; a deputy seized Wenyue on horseback and galloped off, reaching Xiangcheng under cover of darkness.

sentences.zh: 宗龍復分秦兵立營於東南，諸將分壁當賊壘。

translations.literal: Zonglong again divided the Shaanxi troops and established a camp in the southeast; the generals built separate walls facing the bandit stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong redeployed the Shaanxi troops to a camp in the southeast, and the generals built separate walls facing the rebel positions.

sentences.zh: 九日，檄人龍、國奇還兵救，二帥不應。

translations.literal: On the ninth day he issued orders for Renlong and Guoqi to return with their troops to the rescue; the two commanders did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day he sent urgent orders for Renlong and Guoqi to bring their troops back; neither commander answered.

sentences.zh: 宗龍曰：「彼避死，宜不來，吾豈避死哉！

translations.literal: Zonglong said: "They flee death, so of course they will not come—but would I flee death!
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong said: "They are running from death, so of course they won't come—but do you think I will run from death!"

sentences.zh: 」語其麾下曰：「宗龍老矣，今日陷賊中，當與諸軍決一死戰，不能效他人卷甲走也。

translations.literal: " He told his subordinates: "Zonglong is old; today trapped among bandits, I shall fight a decisive battle with you all and cannot imitate others who roll up their armor and flee.
translations.idiomatic: " He told his men: "Zonglong is old; trapped among rebels today, I mean to fight a last battle with you—I will not roll up my armor and flee like the others."

sentences.zh: 」召裨校李本實，即文嶽壁穿塹築壘以拒賊。

translations.literal: " He summoned staff officer Li Benshi to dig through the trench at Wenyue's wall and build ramparts to resist the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned staff officer Li Benshi to break through the trench at Wenyue's abandoned wall and build ramparts against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊亦穿壕二重以圍之。

translations.literal: The bandits also dug double trenches to surround them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dug double trenches of their own to surround the camp.

sentences.zh: 十一日，秦師食盡，宗龍殺馬騾以享軍。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day the Shaanxi army's food was exhausted; Zonglong slaughtered horses and mules to feed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day the Shaanxi army ran out of food; Zonglong slaughtered horses and mules to feed his men.

sentences.zh: 明日，營中馬騾盡，殺賊取其屍分啖之。

translations.literal: The next day the camp's horses and mules were all gone; they killed bandits, took their corpses, and divided the flesh to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day every horse and mule in camp was gone; they killed rebels, took the corpses, and divided the flesh among themselves.

sentences.zh: 十八日，營中火藥、鉛子、矢並盡。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day gunpowder, lead shot, and arrows in the camp were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day gunpowder, shot, and arrows in the camp were all spent.

sentences.zh: 宗龍簡士卒，夷傷死喪之余，有眾六千。

translations.literal: Zonglong selected the troops; after clearing away the wounded and dead, six thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong mustered his men; after clearing away the wounded and dead, six thousand remained.

sentences.zh: 夜半，潛勒諸軍突賊營，殺千余人，潰圍出。

translations.literal: At midnight he secretly led the armies in a surprise attack on the bandit camp, killed more than a thousand, and broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he led a surprise assault on the rebel camp, killed more than a thousand men, and broke out of the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 諸軍星散，宗龍徒步率諸軍且戰且走。

translations.literal: The armies scattered like stars; Zonglong on foot led the troops, fighting as they retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The army scattered in every direction; Zonglong on foot led what remained, fighting as they fled.

sentences.zh: 十九日，日卓午，未至項城八里，賊追及之，執宗龍，呼於門曰：「秦督圍隨官丁也，請啟門納秦督。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day, at noon, still eight li short of Xiangcheng, the bandits overtook them, seized Zonglong, and shouted at the gate: "The Shaanxi governor is surrounded by his attendants; please open the gate and admit the Shaanxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day, at high noon, still eight li from Xiangcheng, the rebels caught up, seized Zonglong, and shouted at the gate: "The Shaanxi governor is here with his escort—open the gate and let him in!"

sentences.zh: 」宗龍大呼曰：「我秦督也，不幸墮賊手，左右皆賊耳。

translations.literal: " Zonglong shouted loudly: "I am the Shaanxi governor; unhappily I have fallen into bandit hands—those beside me are all bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Zonglong shouted: "I am the Shaanxi governor! I have fallen into rebel hands—every man beside me is a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 」賊唾宗龍。

translations.literal: " The bandits spat on Zonglong.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels spat on him.

sentences.zh: 宗龍罵賊曰：「我大臣也，殺則殺耳，豈能為賊賺城以緩死哉！

translations.literal: Zonglong cursed the bandits: "I am a great minister; kill me if you will—how could I trick a city for you bandits to buy a slower death!
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong cursed them: "I am a minister of state—kill me if you will! Do you think I would trick a city open to buy myself a slower death!"

sentences.zh: 」賊抽刀擊宗龍，中其腦而仆，檆其耳鼻死城下。

translations.literal: " The bandits drew knives and struck Zonglong, hitting his brain so that he fell; they cut off his ears and nose and he died below the wall.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels drew their blades and struck him in the head; he fell, and they cut off his ears and nose and left him dead below the wall.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝曰：「若此，可謂樸忠矣。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, the emperor said: "In this way, one may truly be called plain and loyal.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, the emperor said: "In this he showed himself plain and loyal indeed."

sentences.zh: 」復官兵部尚書，加太子少保，謚忠壯，蔭子錦衣世百戶，予祭葬。

translations.literal: " He was posthumously restored as minister of war, given the additional title of junior guardian of the heir apparent, granted the posthumous name Zhongzhuang, his son ennobled as hereditary commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard with one hundred households, and granted sacrificial rites and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: " He was posthumously restored to minister of war, made junior guardian of the heir apparent, given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang (Loyal and Valiant), his son ennobled as hereditary commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard with one hundred households, and granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 人龍、國奇兵潰歸陜，賊遂屠項城。

translations.literal: Renlong and Guoqi's routed troops returned to Shaanxi; the bandits then massacred Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong and Guoqi's shattered troops straggled back to Shaanxi; the rebels then sacked and massacred Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 分兵屠商水、扶溝，遂攻葉縣。

translations.literal: They divided their forces to massacre Shangshui and Fugou, then attacked Yexian.
translations.idiomatic: They sent detachments to massacre Shangshui and Fugou, then attacked Yexian.

sentences.zh: 汪喬年，字歲星，遂安人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiaonian, styled Suixing, was a native of Suian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiaonian, whose courtesy name was Suixing, came from Suian.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice and rose through the ranks to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice and eventually rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年起工部，遷青州知府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was raised in the Ministry of Works and transferred to be prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen he entered the Ministry of Works and was appointed prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以治行卓異，遷登萊兵備副使，乞終養歸。

translations.literal: Because his governance was outstanding, he was transferred to be Deng-Lai military defense vice commissioner, then requested leave to care for his parents until death and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: For outstanding administration he was promoted to Deng-Lai military defense vice commissioner, then asked to retire and care for his parents until their deaths.

sentences.zh: 父喪除，起官平陽，遷陜西右參政，提督學校。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning ended he was raised to office at Pingyang, transferred to right administrative commissioner of Shaanxi, and supervised the schools.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning period ended he was appointed at Pingyang, then transferred to right administrative commissioner of Shaanxi with charge over the schools.

sentences.zh: 再以卓異，就遷按察使。

translations.literal: Again for outstanding merit he was directly promoted to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Again cited for outstanding service, he was promoted directly to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 喬年清若自勵，惡衣菲食，之官，攜二仆，不以家自隨。

translations.literal: Qiaonian was austere and self-disciplined, wearing poor clothes and eating plain food; when he took office he brought only two servants and did not bring his family.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaonian was austere and self-disciplined, dressed plainly and ate sparingly, and when he took office brought only two servants—never his family.

sentences.zh: 為青州，行廊置土銼十余，訟者自炊候鞫，吏無敢索一錢。

translations.literal: As prefect of Qingzhou, in the corridor he set out more than ten earthen stoves; litigants cooked for themselves while awaiting judgment, and clerks dared not demand a single coin.
translations.idiomatic: As Qingzhou prefect he set out more than ten earthen stoves in the corridor so litigants could cook while waiting for their cases; not one clerk dared demand a coin.

sentences.zh: 自負才武，休沐輒馳騎，習弓刀擊刺，寢處風露中。

translations.literal: He prided himself on talent and martial skill; on rest days he would gallop on horseback, practice bow, blade, and thrusting, and sleep in wind and dew.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his martial talent, on his days off he would ride hard, drill with bow and blade, and sleep in the open air.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢右僉都御史，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時李自成已破河南，聲言入關。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng had already overrun Henan and announced he would enter the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had already overrun Henan and was threatening to cross into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 喬年疾驅至商、洛，不見賊。

translations.literal: Qiaonian hurried to Shang and Luo but saw no bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaonian raced to Shangzhou and Luonan but found no rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊圍開封，而三邊總督傅宗龍亦至陜，議抽兵括餉，則關中兵食已盡，無以應。

translations.literal: The bandits besieged Kaifeng, and three-frontiers governor-general Fu Zonglong also reached Shaanxi; when they discussed drawing troops and levying provisions, Guanzhong's military grain was already exhausted and could not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were besieging Kaifeng, and three-frontiers governor-general Fu Zonglong had also reached Shaanxi; when they discussed raising troops and supplies, Guanzhong had nothing left to give.

sentences.zh: 宗龍、喬年握手欷歔而別。

translations.literal: Zonglong and Qiaonian clasped hands, sighed with grief, and parted.
translations.idiomatic: The two men clasped hands, sighed, and went their separate ways.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宗龍敗歿於項城，喬年流涕嘆曰：「傅公死，討賊無人矣。

translations.literal: Before long Zonglong was defeated and died at Xiangcheng; Qiaonian wept and sighed: "Master Fu is dead—there is no one left to suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zonglong was defeated and killed at Xiangcheng; Qiaonian wept and said: "Master Fu is dead—there is no one left to fight the rebels."

sentences.zh: 」已，又聞詔擢喬年兵部右侍郎，總督三邊軍務，代宗龍。

translations.literal: " Soon after he heard an edict promoting Qiaonian to vice minister of war and making him governor-general of the three frontiers in Zonglong's place.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after came word that Qiaonian had been promoted to vice minister of war and appointed governor-general of the three frontiers in Zonglong's place.

sentences.zh: 部檄踵至，趣出關。

translations.literal: Ministry orders arrived in succession, urging him to exit the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry orders arrived one after another, urging him to march out through the pass.

sentences.zh: 是時，關中精銳盡沒於項城。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong's elite troops had all perished at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: By then Guanzhong's best troops had all been destroyed at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 喬年曰：「兵疲餉乏，當方張之寇。

translations.literal: Qiaonian said: "The troops are weary, provisions scarce, and the enemy is at the height of his power.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaonian said: "Our troops are exhausted, our supplies gone, and the enemy is at the height of his power.

sentences.zh: 我出，如以肉餵虎耳。

translations.literal: If I go out, it is like feeding meat to a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: If I march out, I am only feeding meat to a tiger.

sentences.zh: 然不可不一出，以持中原心。

translations.literal: Yet I cannot but go out once, to sustain the heart of the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I must go out at least once, to keep hope alive in the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 」乃收散亡，調邊卒，得馬步三萬人。

translations.literal: " He then gathered the scattered survivors, mobilized frontier troops, and obtained thirty thousand infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " He gathered the scattered survivors, mobilized frontier troops, and mustered thirty thousand infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，率總兵賀人龍、鄭嘉棟、牛成虎出潼關。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year he led regional commanders He Renlong, Zheng Jiadong, and Niu Chenghu out through Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year he led regional commanders He Renlong, Zheng Jiadong, and Niu Chenghu through Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 先是，臨潁為賊守，左良玉破而屠之，盡獲賊所擄。

translations.literal: Earlier Linying was held by bandits; Zuo Liangyu broke it and massacred the place, recovering all the captives the bandits had taken.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the rebels had held Linying; Zuo Liangyu stormed it, massacred the garrison, and recovered all the captives the rebels had taken.

sentences.zh: 自成聞之怒，舍開封而攻良玉，良玉退保郾城，賊圍之急。

translations.literal: Zicheng heard this with rage, abandoned Kaifeng, and attacked Liangyu; Liangyu retreated to defend Yancheng, and the bandits pressed the siege fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng flew into a rage, abandoned Kaifeng, and attacked Liangyu; Liangyu fell back to Yancheng, where the rebels laid siege in force.

sentences.zh: 喬年諸將議曰：「郾城危在旦夕。

translations.literal: Qiaonian and the generals deliberated: "Yancheng is in peril from morning to night.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaonian and his generals debated: "Yancheng may fall at any moment.

sentences.zh: 吾趨郾，賊方銳，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: If we hurry to Yancheng, the bandits are at their sharpest and we will find it hard to contend with them.
translations.idiomatic: If we rush to Yancheng, the rebels are at their peak—we cannot fight them head-on.

sentences.zh: 吾聞襄城距郾四舍，賊老砦鹹在。

translations.literal: I have heard that Xiangcheng is four she from Yancheng, and the bandits' old strongholds are all there.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Xiangcheng lies four stages from Yancheng, and the rebels' old strongholds are all there.

sentences.zh: 吾舍郾而以精銳攻其必應，賊必還兵救，則郾城解矣。

translations.literal: If we abandon Yancheng and with elite troops attack where they must respond, the bandits will certainly return to rescue, and Yancheng will be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave Yancheng and strike their base with our best troops, the rebels will have to turn back—and Yancheng will be saved.

sentences.zh: 郾城解，我擊其前，良玉乘其背，賊可大破也。

translations.literal: Once Yancheng is relieved, we strike their front and Liangyu takes them from behind—the bandits can be greatly broken.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yancheng is relieved, we hit them from the front and Liangyu from the rear—the rebels can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The generals all said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals all agreed: "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 」乃留步兵火器於洛陽，簡精騎萬人兼程進。

translations.literal: " He then left infantry and firearms at Luoyang, selected ten thousand elite cavalry, and advanced day and night.
translations.idiomatic: " He left the infantry and firearms at Luoyang, picked ten thousand crack cavalry, and marched day and night.

sentences.zh: 次郟縣，襄城人張永祺等迎喬年。

translations.literal: He halted at Jia County; Zhang Yongqi of Xiangcheng and others welcomed Qiaonian.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped at Jia County, where Zhang Yongqi of Xiangcheng and others came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 二月二日，喬年入襄城，分人龍、嘉棟、成虎軍三路，駐城東四十里，逼郾城而軍，而自勒兵駐城外。

translations.literal: On the second day of the second month Qiaonian entered Xiangcheng, divided Renlong's, Jiadong's, and Chenghu's armies into three routes, encamped forty li east of the city, pressed toward Yancheng, and himself led troops stationed outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the second month Qiaonian entered Xiangcheng, deployed Renlong, Jiadong, and Chenghu in three columns forty li east of the city facing Yancheng, and himself took command outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 賊果解郾城而救襄城。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed lifted the siege of Yancheng to rescue Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did lift the siege of Yancheng and marched to relieve Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 賊至，三帥奔，良玉救不至，軍大潰。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, the three commanders fled; Liangyu's rescue did not come, and the army collapsed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, all three commanders fled; Liangyu's relief never came, and the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 喬年嘆曰：「此吾死所也。

translations.literal: Qiaonian sighed: "This is where I shall die.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaonian sighed: "This is where I die."

sentences.zh: 」率步卒千余入城守。

translations.literal: " He led more than a thousand infantry into the city to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: " He led more than a thousand infantry into the city to hold it.

sentences.zh: 賊穴地實火藥攻城，喬年亦穿阱，視所鑿，長矛刺之。

translations.literal: The bandits tunneled underground, packed gunpowder, and attacked the walls; Qiaonian also dug pits, watched where they bored, and thrust with long spears.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tunneled under the walls and packed them with gunpowder; Qiaonian dug counter-mines, watched where they dug, and thrust with long spears.

sentences.zh: 賊炮擊喬年坐纛，雉堞盡碎，左右環泣請避之，喬年怒，以足蹴其首曰：「汝畏死，我不畏死也。

translations.literal: Bandit cannon struck Qiaonian's command banner; the parapets were all shattered; those around him wept in a ring and begged him to withdraw; Qiaonian grew angry and kicked their heads with his foot, saying: "You fear death—I do not fear death.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel cannon shattered the parapets around Qiaonian's command banner; his attendants wept and begged him to move; he kicked them and shouted: "You fear death—I do not!"

sentences.zh: 」十七日，城陷，巷戰，殺三賊，自剄不殊，為賊所執，大罵。

translations.literal: " On the seventeenth day the city fell; in street fighting he killed three bandits, cut his own throat but did not die, was seized by bandits, and cursed them loudly.
translations.idiomatic: " On the seventeenth day the city fell; he fought in the streets, killed three rebels, tried to cut his own throat but failed, was seized, and cursed them loudly.

sentences.zh: 賊割其舌，磔殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits cut out his tongue and executed him by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels cut out his tongue and executed him by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 襄城人建祠而祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Xiangcheng built a shrine and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xiangcheng built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 時張國欽、張一貫、黨威、李萬慶及監紀西安同知孫兆祿、材官李可從、襄城知縣曹思正從喬年，皆死之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Guoqin, Zhang Yiguan, Dang Wei, Li Wanqing, and supervising secretary Xi'an subprefectural vice prefect Sun Zhaolu, materiel officer Li Kecong, and Xiangcheng magistrate Cao Sizheng, who had followed Qiaonian, all died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoqin, Zhang Yiguan, Dang Wei, Li Wanqing, supervising secretary and Xi'an vice prefect Sun Zhaolu, materiel officer Li Kecong, and Xiangcheng magistrate Cao Sizheng—all who had followed Qiaonian—died with him.

sentences.zh: 萬慶者，降將射塌天也。

translations.literal: Wanqing was the surrendered general Shetian.
translations.idiomatic: Wanqing was the surrendered general known as Shetian (Collapsing Sky).

sentences.zh: 又有馬帥某者，逸其名。

translations.literal: There was also a certain Commander Ma whose name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a certain Commander Ma whose name has been lost.

sentences.zh: 兆祿，鹽山人。

translations.literal: Zhaolu was a man of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolu came from Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 可從，盩厔人。

translations.literal: Kecong was a man of Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Kecong came from Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 黨威，神木人。

translations.literal: Dang Wei was a man of Shenmu.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Wei came from Shenmu.

sentences.zh: 余莫考。

translations.literal: Of the rest I cannot verify.
translations.idiomatic: I have been unable to verify the rest.

sentences.zh: 黨威則嘗擊賊於西雒峪，擒賊首竇阿婆者也。

translations.literal: Dang Wei had once attacked bandits at Xiluoyu Valley and captured the bandit chieftain Dou Apo.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Wei had once fought rebels at Xiluoyu Valley and captured the chieftain Dou Apo.

sentences.zh: 自成購永祺不得，屠其族，劓刖諸生劉漢臣等百九十人。

translations.literal: Zicheng could not buy Yongqi's capture and massacred his clan, mutilating the student Liu Hanchen and one hundred ninety others.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to capture Yongqi, Zicheng massacred his entire clan and mutilated the student Liu Hanchen and one hundred ninety others.

sentences.zh: 自成數月之間再敗秦師，獲馬二萬，降秦兵又數萬，威震河雒。

translations.literal: Within a few months Zicheng twice defeated the Shaanxi armies, obtained twenty thousand horses, and received the surrender of tens of thousands more Shaanxi troops; his might shook the He and Luo region.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Zicheng twice shattered the Shaanxi armies, seized twenty thousand horses, and accepted the surrender of tens of thousands more Shaanxi troops; his power shook the Yellow and Luo river country.

sentences.zh: 初，喬年之撫陜西也，奉詔發自成先冢。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qiaonian governed Shaanxi, he received an edict to excavate Zicheng's ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qiaonian took office in Shaanxi, he received orders to excavate Li Zicheng's ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 米脂令邊大受，河間靜海舉人，健令也，诇得其族人為縣吏者，掠之。

translations.literal: Mizhi magistrate Bian Dashou, a juren of Jinghai in Hejian, was a vigorous magistrate; he spied out Zicheng's clansmen serving as county clerks and seized them.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi magistrate Bian Dashou, a juren from Jinghai in Hejian, was a forceful administrator; he found Zicheng's kinsmen serving as county clerks and seized them.

sentences.zh: 言：「去縣二百里曰李氏村，亂山中，十六冢環而葬，中其始祖也。

translations.literal: [He] said: "Two hundred li from the county is a place called Li Clan Village, in the chaotic mountains; sixteen tombs are arranged in a ring for burial, and the central one holds their founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Two hundred li from the county lies Li Clan Village, deep in the wild hills. Sixteen graves form a ring—at the center rests their founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 相傳，穴，仙人所定，壙中鐵燈檠，鐵燈不滅，李氏興。

translations.literal: It is handed down that the site, the cave, was set by an immortal; within the chamber was an iron lamp-stand, and if the iron lamp never went out, the Li clan would rise.
translations.idiomatic: Legend held that the spot had been fixed by an immortal. Inside the vault stood an iron lamp-stand; so long as its iron lamp never went out, the Li clan would flourish.

sentences.zh: 」如其言發之螻蟻數石，火光熒熒然。

translations.literal: " Following his words they opened it; ants poured out in several shi, and the firelight flickered brightly.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on this account, they opened the tomb. Ants swarmed out by the shihu-load, and a pale fire glowed within.

sentences.zh: 檆棺，骨青黑，被體黃毛，腦後穴大如錢，赤蛇盤，三四寸，角而飛，高丈許，咋咋吞日光者六七，反而伏。

translations.literal: [It was] a catalpa-wood coffin; the bones were greenish black, covered over the body with yellow hair; behind the skull was a hole as large as a coin, around which a red serpent coiled—three or four cun; horned, it flew up, rising about a zhang; six or seven times it snapped and swallowed the sunlight, then turned back and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: Within was a catalpa coffin. The bones had turned green-black, the corpse clothed in yellow hair. At the back of the skull gaped a hole the size of a coin, around which coiled a red serpent some three or four cun long. Horned, it took wing and rose a zhang into the air, snapping and gulping at the sunlight six or seven times before wheeling back to settle down.

sentences.zh: 喬年函其顱骨、臘蛇以聞，焚其余，雜以穢，棄之。

translations.literal: Qiaonian placed the skull bone and the preserved serpent in a casket to report [to the throne]; he burned the remainder, mixed it with filth, and discarded it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaonian boxed the skull and the preserved serpent and sent word to the court. The rest he burned, mingled with refuse, and threw away.

sentences.zh: 自成聞之，嚙齒大恨曰：「吾必致死於喬年。

translations.literal: Zicheng heard of it, gnashed his teeth in great hatred, and said: "I must bring about Qiaonian's death!
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng heard the news, he gnashed his teeth in fury and swore: "Qiaonian shall surely die by my hand!

sentences.zh: 」既殺喬年，由西華攻陳州。

translations.literal: " After he had killed Qiaonian, he advanced from Xihua to attack Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After he killed Qiaonian, he marched from Xihua to attack Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楊文嶽，字鬥望，南充人。

translations.literal: Yang Wenyue, courtesy name Douwang, was a native of Nanchong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wenyue, styled Douwang, came from Nanchong.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十七年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-seventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: Appointed as Xingren.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed bearer of credentials at court.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年，擢兵科給事中，屢遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi, he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Office of Military Affairs, and repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Office of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianqi he rose to supervising secretary in the Office of Military Affairs and was later promoted to chief supervising secretary in the Office of Rites.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，出為江西右參政，歷湖廣、廣西按察使，雲南、山西左右布政使，以右副都御史巡撫登、萊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, he went out to serve as right provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi; he successively served as provincial surveillance commissioner of Huguang and Guangxi, left and right provincial administration commissioners of Yunnan and Shanxi, and as right vice censor-in-chief to pacify Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen he was posted as Jiangxi's deputy administrative commissioner; he then served as provincial surveillance commissioner in Huguang and Guangxi, as left and right administration commissioner in Yunnan and Shanxi, and finally as right vice censor-in-chief governing Dengzhou and Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年擢兵部右侍郎，總督保定、山東、河北軍務，代孫傳庭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to vice minister of the Right in the Ministry of War, and as grand coordinator took charge of military affairs in Baoding, Shandong, and Hebei, replacing Sun Chuanting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was elevated to vice minister of the Right in the Ministry of War and appointed grand coordinator of Baoding, Shandong, and Hebei, succeeding Sun Chuanting.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，李自成陷洛陽，犯開封，文嶽率總兵虎大威以眾二萬赴救。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year, Li Zicheng took Luoyang and threatened Kaifeng; Wenyue led the commander-in-chief Hu Dawei with twenty thousand men to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year Li Zicheng seized Luoyang and pressed Kaifeng; Wenyue marched to the rescue with the commander Hu Dawei and twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 渡河，賊先遁，追擊於鳴臯。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, the rebels fled first; he pursued and struck them at Minggao.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river he found the rebels already in flight and chased them to Minggao.

sentences.zh: 還，駐兵開封。

translations.literal: Returning, he encamped his troops at Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew and stationed his army at Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 疫作，乃頓兵於汝寧，出屯西平、新蔡間。

translations.literal: When plague broke out, he halted his army at Runing and went out to camp between Xiping and Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: When epidemic disease spread, he halted at Runing and deployed between Xiping and Xincai.

sentences.zh: 七月，自成走內鄉、淅川，與羅汝才合。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Zicheng fled to Neixiang and Xichuan and joined with Luo Rucai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zicheng withdrew toward Neixiang and Xichuan and joined forces with Luo Rucai.

sentences.zh: 文嶽趨鄧州，自成還攻之。

translations.literal: Wenyue hastened to Dengzhou; Zicheng turned back to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue rushed toward Dengzhou, and Zicheng wheeled back to attack him.

sentences.zh: 文嶽戰三捷，斬其魁一條龍、一只龍，賊遁去。

translations.literal: Wenyue fought three victories, beheaded their chiefs Yitiao Long and Yizhi Long, and the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue won three successive battles, killing the rebel leaders Yitiao Long and Yizhi Long, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九月，會陜西總督傅宗龍於新蔡，與賊遇，大潰於孟家莊，再潰於火燒店。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he joined Shaanxi governor Fu Zonglong at Xincai, met the rebels, and was routed at Mengjia Village and again at Huoshaodian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he joined Shaanxi governor Fu Zonglong at Xincai; they met the rebels and suffered crushing defeats at Mengjia Village and again at Huoshaodian.

sentences.zh: 部將挾文嶽夜入於項城。

translations.literal: A subordinate general took Wenyue under cover of night into Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: One of his subordinates led Wenyue into Xiangcheng under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 明日奔陳州，宗龍遂覆沒。

translations.literal: The next day he fled to Chen Prefecture, and Zonglong was completely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wenyue fled to Chen Prefecture while Zonglong's force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 事聞，文嶽革職，充為事官，戴罪自贖。

translations.literal: When the report reached the court, Wenyue was dismissed from office, reduced to an official-at-large, and ordered to redeem his fault through service.
translations.idiomatic: News of the disaster reached the capital; Wenyue was stripped of rank, reduced to a nominal post, and ordered to atone through further service.

sentences.zh: 乃收集散亡，率所部就巡撫高名衡防杞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered the scattered and the lost, led his own troops to join Pacification Commissioner Gao Mingheng in defending Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He then rallied the scattered remnants and joined Pacification Commissioner Gao Mingheng in the defense of Qi County.

sentences.zh: 賊遂破葉縣，拔泌陽，乘勝陷南陽，殺唐王，下鄧州等十四城，再圍開封。

translations.literal: The rebels then broke Ye County, took Biyang, and riding victory seized Nanyang, killed the Prince of Tang, captured fourteen cities including Dengzhou, and again besieged Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels went on to storm Ye County and Biyang, then seized Nanyang in the wake of victory, killed the Prince of Tang, took fourteen cities including Dengzhou, and once again besieged Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，文嶽馳救開封，論功復官。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Wenyue raced to relieve Kaifeng; his merit was assessed and his office restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year Wenyue hurried to Kaifeng's relief and was reinstated on merit.

sentences.zh: 臨潁為賊守，左良玉破而屠之，退保郾城。

translations.literal: Linying was held by the rebels; Zuo Liangyu broke it and massacred it, then withdrew to defend Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Linying until Zuo Liangyu stormed it and put the city to the sword, then fell back to defend Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 自成圍郾城。

translations.literal: Zicheng besieged Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng then laid siege to Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，督師丁啟睿及文嶽、大威救郾城。

translations.literal: In the second month, Grand Secretary Ding Qirui together with Wenyue and Dawei went to relieve Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Grand Secretary Ding Qirui, Wenyue, and Dawei marched to relieve Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 賊潰，距官軍數里而營。

translations.literal: The rebels broke and fled, then encamped several li from the government army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and withdrew, pitching camp a few li from the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 文嶽、啟睿相掎角，持十一晝夜。

translations.literal: Wenyue and Qirui supported each other like pincers and held their ground for eleven day-and-nights.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue and Qirui coordinated in a pincer formation and held for eleven days and nights.

sentences.zh: 總督汪喬年出關，賊引去，再攻開封。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Qiaonian came out through the pass; the rebels drew off and again attacked Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Wang Qiaonian marched out through the pass, the rebels withdrew and renewed their assault on Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔起侯恂兵部右侍郎，總督保定、山東、河南、湖北軍務，代文嶽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month an edict recalled Hou Xun as vice minister of the Right in the Ministry of War, to serve as grand coordinator over Baoding, Shandong, Henan, and Hubei military affairs, replacing Wenyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the throne recalled Hou Xun as vice minister of the Right in the Ministry of War and appointed him grand coordinator over Baoding, Shandong, Henan, and Hubei, in Wenyue's place.

sentences.zh: 命所司察文嶽罪狀。

translations.literal: The relevant offices were ordered to investigate Wenyue's offenses.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered an inquiry into Wenyue's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 七月朔，文嶽、啟睿合良玉、大威及楊德政、方國安四總兵之師，次朱仙鎮。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, Wenyue and Qirui combined the forces of four commander-in-chiefs—Liangyu, Dawei, Yang Dezheng, and Fang Guo'an—and halted at Zhuxian Town.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month Wenyue and Qirui assembled the armies of four regional commanders—Liangyu, Dawei, Yang Dezheng, and Fang Guo'an—and encamped at Zhuxian Town.

sentences.zh: 諸軍盡潰，啟睿、文嶽奔汝寧。

translations.literal: All the armies were completely routed; Qirui and Wenyue fled to Runing.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies collapsed entirely; Qirui and Wenyue fled to Runing.

sentences.zh: 賊渡河，追奔四百里，官軍失亡數萬。

translations.literal: The rebels crossed the river, pursued the fleeing army for four hundred li, and the government army lost tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed the river and chased the fugitives four hundred li, costing the imperial army tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 詔褫官候勘。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him of office pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed him from office pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 九月，文嶽在汝寧，夜襲賊營有功。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wenyue was at Runing; a night raid on the rebel camp achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, still at Runing, Wenyue scored success with a night attack on the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 賊既灌開封，旋敗孫傳庭兵，以閏十一月悉眾薄汝寧，老回回、革裏眼、左金王等畢會。

translations.literal: After the rebels had flooded Kaifeng, they soon defeated Sun Chuanting's army; in the intercalary eleventh month they brought their full strength against Runing, and Lao Huikai, Ge Liyan, Zuo Jinwang, and others all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had inundated Kaifeng, the rebels soon routed Sun Chuanting's army; in the intercalary eleventh month they moved their entire force against Runing, and rebel chiefs including Lao Huikai, Ge Liyan, and Zuo Jinwang all rallied there.

sentences.zh: 文嶽遣都司康世德以輕騎偵賊，世德走還汝，將其步騎五百，夜縱火噪而奔。

translations.literal: Wenyue sent Assistant Commander Kang Shide with light cavalry to scout the rebels; Shide fled back to Ru, took five hundred infantry and cavalry, and in the night set fires, raised a clamor, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue dispatched Assistant Commander Kang Shide with light cavalry to reconnoiter the rebels, but Shide fled back to Ru with five hundred foot and horse soldiers, firing the camp and raising an uproar as he ran.

sentences.zh: 十三日，群賊並至，壓汝寧五里而軍。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day the rebel bands all arrived and encamped five li from Runing.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth the rebel hosts converged and pitched camp five li from Runing.

sentences.zh: 監軍僉事孔貞會以川兵屯城東，文嶽以保兵屯城西。

translations.literal: Military Supervisor Secretariat Member Kong Zhenhui encamped with Sichuan troops east of the city; Wenyue encamped with Baoding troops west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Military Supervisor Kong Zhenhui held the east wall with Sichuan troops, while Wenyue posted Baoding soldiers on the west.

sentences.zh: 賊兵進攻，相持一晝夜。

translations.literal: The rebel soldiers pressed the attack; the two sides held one day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed the assault and the two sides battled through the day and night.

sentences.zh: 川兵潰，殺傷數百。

translations.literal: The Sichuan troops broke; several hundred were killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan detachment collapsed, with several hundred killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 賊奪其馬騾，悉眾攻保兵，漸不支。

translations.literal: The rebels seized their horses and mules and brought their full force against the Baoding troops, who gradually could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized their horses and mules, then hurled the whole host against the Baoding troops, who slowly gave way.

sentences.zh: 僉事王世琮、知府傅汝為、通判朱國寶縋將士入城，副將賈悌、參將馮名聖亦掖文嶽、貞會登城。

translations.literal: Secretariat Member Wang Shizong, Prefect Fu Ruwei, and Assistant Prefect Zhu Guobao lowered troops into the city with ropes; Vice Commander Jia Ti and Assistant Commander Feng Mingsheng also supported Wenyue and Zhenhui up onto the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Member Wang Shizong, Prefect Fu Ruwei, and Assistant Prefect Zhu Guobao hauled soldiers into the city by rope; Vice Commander Jia Ti and Assistant Commander Feng Mingsheng also helped Wenyue and Zhenhui climb the wall to safety.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊四面環攻，戴扉以陣，矢石雲梯堵墻而立。

translations.literal: The next day the rebels attacked on all four sides, forming ranks behind shields; arrows, stones, cloud-ladders, and scaling equipment piled against the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels assaulted from every side, advancing behind shield walls in formation; arrows, stones, siege ladders, and scaling gear massed against the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 城頭矢炮擂石雨集，賊死傷山積，而攻不休。

translations.literal: From atop the wall arrows, cannon, and rolling stones fell like rain; rebel dead and wounded piled like hills, yet the attack did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: From the battlements a storm of arrows, cannon shot, and rolling stones poured down; rebel corpses heaped up like hills, yet the assault never stopped.

sentences.zh: 一鼓百道並登，執文嶽及世琮、國寶、悌、名聖於城頭，殺汝陽知縣文師頤於城上。

translations.literal: At one drumbeat a hundred routes scaled together; they seized Wenyue together with Shizong, Guobao, Ti, and Mingsheng on the wall-top and killed Ruyang magistrate Wen Shiyi on the rampart.
