translations.idiomatic: At a single drumstroke a hundred assault columns scaled the walls together; they captured Wenyue along with Shizong, Guobao, Ti, and Mingsheng on the ramparts and killed Ruyang magistrate Wen Shiyi on the wall.

sentences.zh: 汝為聞變，赴水死。

translations.literal: Ruwei, hearing the disaster, went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruwei heard what had happened, he drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 賊擁文嶽等見自成，大罵，賊怒，縛之城南三里鋪，以大炮擊之，洞胸糜骨而死。

translations.literal: The rebels brought Wenyue and the others before Zicheng; they cursed him greatly; the rebels were enraged, bound them at Sanlipu south of the city, and struck them with great cannon until their chests were pierced and their bones pulverized—they died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dragged Wenyue and the others before Zicheng; they reviled him in fury, and the rebels, enraged, bound them at Sanlipu south of the city and blasted them with heavy cannon until their chests were torn open and their bones shattered.

sentences.zh: 士民屠戮數萬，焚公私廨舍殆盡。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners were slaughtered by the tens of thousands; public and private offices and dwellings were burned nearly to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of officials and townspeople were put to the sword, and nearly every public and private building was burned.

sentences.zh: 貞會執去，不知所終。

translations.literal: Zhenhui was seized and taken away; his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenhui was taken captive; nothing is known of his fate afterward.

sentences.zh: 自成以文嶽死忠，備禮斂之。

translations.literal: Zicheng, considering that Wenyue had died loyal, prepared full rites and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng honored Wenyue's loyalty in death and gave him a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 遂拔營走確山、信陽、泌陽，向襄陽，虜崇王由樻、崇世子、諸王妃及河南懷安諸王以行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he broke camp and went toward Queshan, Xinyang, and Biyang, heading for Xiangyang; he carried off Prince Chong Youyu, the Chong heir apparent, the various consorts, and the Princes of Huai'an and others of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then broke camp and marched toward Queshan, Xinyang, and Biyang on the road to Xiangyang, taking Prince Chong Youyu, the heir apparent, the consorts, and the Princes of Huai'an and other Henan princes with them as captives.

sentences.zh: 汝為，字於宣，江陵人。

translations.literal: Ruwei, courtesy name Yuxuan, was a native of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ruwei, styled Yuxuan, came from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventh year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 世琮，字仲發，達州人。

translations.literal: Shizong, courtesy name Zhongfa, was a native of Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizong, styled Zhongfa, came from Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 國寶，成都人。

translations.literal: Guobao was a native of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guobao was from Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 師頤，全州人。

translations.literal: Shiyi was a native of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shiyi came from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 皆舉人。

translations.literal: All were juren.
translations.idiomatic: All four had passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 世琮嘗為汝寧推官，討土寇，流矢貫耳不為動，時號王鐵耳者也。

translations.literal: Shizong had once served as Runing pushing officer; suppressing local bandits, a stray arrow pierced his ear and he did not stir—at the time he was called Wang Iron Ear.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had once served as Runing's assistant magistrate; while subduing local bandits an arrow drove through his ear without making him flinch, earning him the nickname Iron-Eared Wang.

sentences.zh: 師頤蒞任甫三日。

translations.literal: Shiyi had taken office only three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi had been in office barely three days.

sentences.zh: 孫傳庭，字百雅，代州振武衛人。

translations.literal: Sun Chuanting, courtesy name Baiya, was a native of Zhenwu Guard in Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuanting, styled Baiya, came from Zhenwu Guard in Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 自父以上，四世舉於鄉。

translations.literal: From his father upward, four generations had passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: For four generations, from his father upward, the family had produced provincial graduates.

sentences.zh: 傳庭儀表頎碩，沈毅多籌略。

translations.literal: Chuanting's bearing was tall and imposing; he was deep, resolute, and rich in stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting was tall and commanding in appearance, sober and resolute, and richly supplied with plans.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十七年成進士，授永城知縣，以才調商丘。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination; appointed magistrate of Yongcheng, he was transferred for talent to Shangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the forty-seventh year of Wanli, served first as magistrate of Yongcheng, and was transferred to Shangqiu on account of his ability.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，擢吏部驗封主事，屢遷稽勛郎中，請告歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel for seals and patents, was repeatedly promoted to bureau director of meritorious service, and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he rose to principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel's Seals Bureau, was promoted to bureau director in the Meritorious Service Office, and then retired on leave.

sentences.zh: 家居久不出。

translations.literal: He remained at home for a long time without emerging.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed at home for many years without taking office again.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年秋，始遷驗封郎中，超遷順天府丞。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year of Chongzhen he was finally transferred to bureau director of the Seals Office and was abruptly promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year of Chongzhen he was at last recalled as bureau director in the Seals Office and then leapfrogged to vice prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 陜西巡撫甘學闊不能討賊，秦之士大夫嘩於朝，乃推邊才用傳庭，以九年三月受代。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner Gan Xuekuo could not suppress the rebels; the gentry of Qin clamored at court, whereupon border talent was sought and Chuanting was chosen; in the third month of the ninth year he succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner Gan Xuekuo failed to subdue the rebels, and Qin gentry raised an uproar at court; border talent was sought out and Chuanting was chosen, succeeding to office in the third month of the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 傳庭蒞秦，嚴征發期會，一從軍興法。

translations.literal: When Chuanting arrived in Qin, he enforced strict levies and deadlines, following entirely the wartime regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chuanting took charge in Qin, he enforced strict levies and rigid deadlines under the full wartime code.

sentences.zh: 秦人愛之不如總督洪承疇，然其才自足辦賊。

translations.literal: The people of Qin loved him less than Governor Hong Chengchou, yet his talent alone was sufficient to manage the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shaanxi liked him less than Governor Hong Chengchou, but his talent was more than enough to deal with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊首整齊王據商、雒，諸將不敢攻，檄副將羅尚文擊斬之。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftain King Zhengqi held Shang and Luo; the generals dared not attack; [Chuanting] issued an order to Vice Commander Luo Shangwen to strike and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chieftain King Zhengqi held Shangzhou and Luozhou, and no general dared move against him until Chuanting ordered Vice Commander Luo Shangwen to attack and kill him.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊亂關中，有名字者以十數，高迎祥最強，拓養坤黨最眾，所謂闖王、蠍子塊者也。

translations.literal: At that time rebels ravaged Guanzhong; those with names numbered more than ten; Gao Yingxiang was strongest, and Tuo Yangkun's faction was largest—the so-called Dash King and Scorpion Lump.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits ravaged Guanzhong; a dozen or more had made names for themselves. Gao Yingxiang was the strongest, Tuo Yangkun commanded the largest following—the famed Dash King and Scorpion Lump.

sentences.zh: 傳庭設方略，親擊迎祥於盩厔之黑水峪，擒之，及其偽領哨黃龍、總管劉哲，獻俘闕下。

translations.literal: Chuanting devised strategy and personally struck Yingxiang at Heishui Valley in Zhouzhi, captured him together with his false lead scout Huang Long and steward Liu Zhe, and presented the captives below the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting laid his plans and personally struck Yingxiang at Heishui Valley in Zhouzhi, capturing him along with the rebel scout Huang Long and chief of staff Liu Zhe, and sent the prisoners to the capital.

sentences.zh: 錄功，增秩一等。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and his rank was raised one degree.
translations.idiomatic: His victory was entered on the rolls of merit and his rank was raised one step.

sentences.zh: 而賊黨自是乃共推李自成為闖王矣。

translations.literal: From that point the rebel bands together elevated Li Zicheng as Dash King.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the rebel bands united in proclaiming Li Zicheng the Dash King.

sentences.zh: 明年，養坤及其黨張耀文來降。

translations.literal: The next year Yangkun and his follower Zhang Yaowen came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yangkun and his lieutenant Zhang Yaowen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 已而養坤叛去，諭其下追斬之。

translations.literal: Before long Yangkun rebelled and fled away; [Chuanting] instructed his subordinates to pursue and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yangkun rebelled and fled, whereupon Chuanting ordered his men to hunt him down and kill him.

sentences.zh: 擊賊惠登相於涇陽、三原，登相西走。

translations.literal: He struck the rebel Hui Dengxiang at Jingyang and Sanyuan; Dengxiang fled west.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the rebel Hui Dengxiang at Jingyang and Sanyuan, driving Dengxiang westward.

sentences.zh: 河南賊馬進忠、劉國能等十七部入渭南，追之出關，復合河南兵夾擊之，先後斬首千余級。

translations.literal: Seventeen bands of Henan rebels—Ma Jinzhong, Liu Guoneng, and others—entered Weinan; he pursued them out of the pass and again combined with Henan troops to strike from both sides, beheading more than a thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen Henan rebel bands led by Ma Jinzhong and Liu Guoneng invaded Weinan; he chased them out through the pass, then joined Henan troops in a pincer attack, taking more than a thousand heads in successive clashes.

sentences.zh: 進忠等復擾商、雒、藍田，叛卒與之合，將犯西安。

translations.literal: Jinzhong and the others again harassed Shang, Luo, and Lantian; mutinous soldiers joined them and were about to invade Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong and his fellows renewed their raids on Shangzhou, Luozhou, and Lantian; mutineers rallied to them and prepared to strike Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 遣左光先、曹變蛟追走之渭南，降其渠一條龍，招還脅從。

translations.literal: He sent Zuo Guangxian and Cao Bianjiao to pursue them and drive them off at Weinan, induced their chieftain Yitiao Long to surrender, and recalled those who had been coerced to follow.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zuo Guangxian and Cao Bianjiao to drive them from Weinan, accepted the surrender of the chieftain Yitiao Long, and win back those who had followed under duress.

sentences.zh: 募健兒擊余賊，斬聖世王、瓦背、一翅飛，降鎮天王、上山虎，又殲白捍賊渠魁數人。

translations.literal: He recruited stalwart men to strike the remaining rebels, beheaded Shengshi Wang, Wabei, and Yichi Fei, induced Zhen Tianwang and Shangshan Hu to surrender, and also destroyed several chiefs of the White Club rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He raised crack troops against the remaining rebels, killing Shengshi Wang, Wabei, and Yichi Fei, accepting the surrender of Zhen Tianwang and Shangshan Hu, and wiping out several chiefs of the White Club band.

sentences.zh: 關南稍靖。

translations.literal: The south of the Pass grew somewhat tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Pass the country grew somewhat quieter.

sentences.zh: 遣副將盛略等敗賊大天王於寶雞，賊走入山谷，傳庭追之鳳翔。

translations.literal: He sent Vice Commander Sheng Lue and others to defeat the rebel Great Heavenly King at Baoji; the rebels fled into the valleys and Chuanting pursued them to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Vice Commander Sheng Lue and others to rout the rebel Great Heavenly King at Baoji; the rebels fled into the hills and Chuanting chased them as far as Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 他賊出棧道，謀越關犯河南，還軍擊，賊走伏斜谷，復大敗之，降其余眾。

translations.literal: Other rebels came out by the plank roads and planned to cross the Pass and invade Henan; he turned his army back to strike; the rebels fled and hid in Xie Valley; he again inflicted a great defeat and induced the remainder to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Other rebels emerged from the plank roads intending to cross the Pass into Henan; he wheeled his army back, drove them into Xie Valley, crushed them again, and took the survivors' surrender.

sentences.zh: 西安四衛，舊有屯軍二萬四千，田二萬余頃，其後田歸豪右，軍盡虛籍。

translations.literal: The four guards of Xi'an originally had twenty-four thousand garrison troops and more than twenty thousand qing of fields; afterward the fields passed to great families and the military rolls were entirely hollow.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'an's four guards once fielded twenty-four thousand garrison troops on more than twenty thousand qing of farmland, but later the land passed to powerful families while the rolls listed phantom soldiers.

sentences.zh: 傳庭厘得軍萬一千有奇，歲收屯課銀十四萬五千余兩，米麥萬三千五百余石。

translations.literal: Chuanting sorted out and recovered more than eleven thousand troops; each year the garrison levy yielded more than one hundred forty-five thousand taels of silver and more than thirteen thousand five hundred shi of grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting recovered a usable force of just over eleven thousand men, yielding annual garrison revenues of more than 145,000 taels of silver and 13,500 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，增秩，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; [Chuanting's] rank was increased and silver and silks were bestowed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, raised his rank, and rewarded him with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 會楊嗣昌入為本兵，條上方略。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Sichang entered office as minister of the Ministry of War and submitted his strategic plan in articles.
translations.idiomatic: About then Yang Sichang became minister of War and submitted a comprehensive strategic plan.

sentences.zh: 洪承疇以秦督兼剿務，而用廣撫熊文燦為總理。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou, as governor of Qin, also took on suppression duties, while Huguang Pacification Commissioner Xiong Wencan was appointed overall coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou, governor of Shaanxi, was given joint responsibility for suppression, and Huguang Pacification Commissioner Xiong Wencan was made overall coordinator.

sentences.zh: 分四正六隅，馬三步七，計兵十二萬，加派至二百八十萬，期百日平賊。

translations.literal: Dividing into four fronts and six corners, with three parts cavalry and seven parts infantry, the plan totaled one hundred twenty thousand troops; levies were increased to two million eight hundred thousand [taels], with a hundred-day deadline to pacify the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The plan divided the campaign into four cardinal fronts and six supporting sectors, three-tenths cavalry to seven-tenths infantry, totaling 120,000 troops; fresh levies were imposed worth 2.8 million taels, with a hundred-day deadline to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 傳庭移書爭之，曰：「無益，且非特此也。

translations.literal: Chuanting sent a dispatch arguing against it, saying: "It will be useless—and not only for this reason alone.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting wrote in protest: "It will do no good—and that is not the only problem.

sentences.zh: 部卒屢經潰蹶，民力竭矣，恐不堪命。

translations.literal: The troops have repeatedly been routed and broken; the people's strength is exhausted—I fear they cannot bear the command.
translations.idiomatic: The troops have been broken again and again, and the people are exhausted; I fear they cannot sustain such demands.

sentences.zh: 必欲行之，賊不必盡，而害中於國家。

translations.literal: If it must be carried out, the rebels need not all be destroyed before the harm falls on the state itself.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on pushing this through, the rebels may not be wiped out before the state itself is grievously harmed.

sentences.zh: 」累數千言，嗣昌大忤。

translations.literal: " [The letter] ran to several thousand characters; Sichang was greatly offended.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran to several thousand words—and Sichang took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 部議，秦撫當一正面，募土著萬人，給餉銀二十三萬，以商、雒等處為汛守。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated: the Qin governor should take one cardinal front, recruit ten thousand local troops, allocate two hundred thirty thousand taels in rations silver, and use Shang, Luo, and other places as garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry decided that the Shaanxi governor should hold one of the four cardinal fronts, raise ten thousand local troops, supply 230,000 taels in pay, and garrison Shangzhou, Luonan, and the surrounding districts.

sentences.zh: 傳庭知其不可用也，乃核帑藏，蠲贖鍰，得銀四萬八千，市馬募兵，自辦滅賊具，不用部議。

translations.literal: Chuanting knew it could not be used; he then audited the treasury stores, remitted redemption fines, obtained forty-eight thousand taels of silver, bought horses and recruited troops, and furnished his own means to destroy the rebels, not using the ministry's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting saw that the plan was unworkable. He audited the provincial coffers, remitted redemption fines, raised 48,000 taels, bought horses, recruited soldiers, and equipped a suppression force on his own—without relying on the ministry's scheme.

sentences.zh: 會諸撫報募兵及額，傳庭疏獨不至。

translations.literal: Just then all the governors reported that recruited troops had reached quota; Chuanting's memorial alone did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: About then every governor reported that recruitment quotas had been met—only Chuanting's memorial had not come in.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌言軍法不行於秦，自請白衣領職，以激帝怒。

translations.literal: Sichang said military law could not be enforced in Qin and asked to serve in plain clothes to provoke the emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang declared that military law could not be enforced in Shaanxi and offered to serve in undress as a way to stir the emperor's wrath against Chuanting.

sentences.zh: 傳庭奏曰：「使臣如他撫，籍郡縣民兵上之，遂謂及額，則臣先所報屯兵已及額矣。

translations.literal: Chuanting memorialized, saying: "If your subject were like the other governors, listing county and district militia and reporting them upward, then calling it reaching quota—then the garrison troops I reported earlier would already have reached quota.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting replied in a memorial: "If I were like the other governors—simply tallying county militia and reporting them as recruits—then the garrison troops I had already reported would count as meeting the quota.

sentences.zh: 況更有募練馬步軍，數且逾萬，何嘗不遵部議。

translations.literal: Moreover there are additionally recruited and trained mounted and foot armies, their number exceeding ten thousand—when have I failed to follow the ministry's plan?
translations.idiomatic: And I have besides recruited and drilled cavalry and infantry numbering more than ten thousand—how can you say I have not followed the ministry's plan?

sentences.zh: 至百日之期，商、雒之汛守，臣皆不敢委。

translations.literal: As for the hundred-day deadline, the garrison duties at Shang and Luo—I dare not shirk any of them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the hundred-day deadline and the garrison posts at Shangzhou and Luonan, I have not shirked a single duty.

sentences.zh: 然使賊入商、雒，而臣不能禦，則治臣罪。

translations.literal: Yet if rebels enter Shang and Luo and your subject cannot repel them, then punish your subject.
translations.idiomatic: But if rebels break into Shangzhou or Luonan and I fail to stop them, then hold me accountable.

sentences.zh: 若臣扼商、雒，而逾期不能滅賊，誤剿事者必非臣。

translations.literal: If your subject holds Shang and Luo yet past the deadline cannot destroy the rebels, the one who bungles the suppression campaign will surely not be your subject.
translations.idiomatic: If I hold Shangzhou and Luonan yet the rebels are not destroyed by the deadline, the failure will not be mine.

sentences.zh: 」嗣昌無以難，然銜之彌甚。

translations.literal: " Sichang had no way to refute him, yet bore a grudge against him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang could find no answer—but his resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 傳庭兩奉詔進秩，當加部銜，嗣昌抑弗奏。

translations.literal: Chuanting twice received edicts to advance in rank and should have been given a ministry title; Sichang suppressed it and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting twice received imperial orders to advance in rank and was due a ministry title, but Sichang blocked the recommendation and never submitted it.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，賊破漢陰、石泉，則坐傳庭失援，削其所加秩。

translations.literal: In spring of the eleventh year, when rebels took Hanyin and Shiquan, Chuanting was held responsible for failing to send relief, and the rank added to him was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year, after rebels overran Hanyin and Shiquan, Chuanting was blamed for failing to relieve them and stripped of the rank he had been granted.

sentences.zh: 傳庭出扼商、雒。

translations.literal: Chuanting went out to block Shang and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting marched out to hold Shangzhou and Luonan.

sentences.zh: 大天王等犯慶陽、寶雞，還軍戰合水，破走之，獲其二子，追擊之延安。

translations.literal: The Great Heavenly King and others invaded Qingyang and Baoji; [Chuanting] turned the army back and fought at Heshui, routed them, captured two of his sons, and pursued them to Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Heavenly King and his followers struck Qingyang and Baoji, Chuanting wheeled his army about, fought them at Heshui, routed them, captured two of the rebel leader's sons, and chased them as far as Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 過天星、混天星等從徽、秦趨鳳翔，逼澄城。

translations.literal: Guo Tianxing, Hun Tianxing, and others moved from Huizhou and Qinzhou toward Fengxiang and pressed upon Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tianxing, Hun Tianxing, and their bands advanced from Huizhou and Qinzhou toward Fengxiang and threatened Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 傳庭分兵五道擊之楊家嶺、黃龍山，大破之，斬首二千余級。

translations.literal: Chuanting divided troops into five routes and attacked them at Yangjialing and Huanglong Mountain, crushing them and taking more than two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting split his force into five columns and struck them at Yangjialing and Huanglong Mountain, winning a crushing victory and claiming more than two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 大天王知二子不殺，遂降。

translations.literal: The Great Heavenly King, learning his two sons were not killed, then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Heavenly King learned that his two sons had been spared, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 賊引而北，犯延安。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew northward and invaded Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pulled back north and raided Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 傳庭策鄜州西、合水東三四百里，荒山邃谷，賊入當自斃，乃率標兵中部遏其東，檄變蛟、慶陽拒其西，伏兵三水、淳化間。

translations.literal: Chuanting planned that west of Fuzhou and east of Heshui lay three or four hundred li of barren mountains and deep valleys—rebels entering would destroy themselves; he then led banner troops in the center to block their east, sent dispatches to Bian Jiao and Qingyang to hold their west, and placed ambush troops between Sanshui and Chunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting reckoned that the three or four hundred li west of Fuzhou and east of Heshui—wild mountains and deep ravines—would be a death trap for any rebel force. He led his banner troops to block the east, ordered Bian Jiao and the Qingyang garrison to hold the west, and hid troops in ambush between Sanshui and Chunhua.

sentences.zh: 賊饑，出掠食，則大張旗幟，鳴鼓角以邀之，一日夜馳二百五十里。

translations.literal: When the rebels grew hungry and came out to plunder food, [he] unfurled banners on a grand scale and sounded drums and horns to challenge them, riding two hundred fifty li in one day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When hunger drove the rebels out to forage, he unfurled his banners, sounded drums and horns in challenge, and rode two hundred fifty li in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 賊大驚，西奔，至職田莊，遇伏而敗；

translations.literal: The rebels were greatly alarmed and fled west; reaching Zhitianzhuang they met ambush and were defeated;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels panicked and fled west; at Zhitianzhuang they ran into an ambush and were broken;

sentences.zh: 復走寶雞，取棧道，再中伏大敗；

translations.literal: They fled again to Baoji and took the plank road, again meeting ambush and suffering a great defeat;
translations.idiomatic: they retreated toward Baoji and took the plank road, only to walk into another ambush and suffer a second rout;

sentences.zh: 折而走隴州關山道，又為伏兵所挫。

translations.literal: They turned and went by the Longzhou Guanshan road, and were again struck down by ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: they turned onto the Longzhou Guanshan road and were cut down by ambush troops once more.

sentences.zh: 三敗，賊死者無算，過天星、混天星並降。

translations.literal: After three defeats, rebel dead were beyond counting; Guo Tianxing and Hun Tianxing both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After three defeats the rebel dead were beyond count, and both Guo Tianxing and Hun Tianxing surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又逐賊邠、寧間，陷陣，獲其渠。

translations.literal: Again pursuing the rebels between Bin and Ning, [he] broke through the formation and captured their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels again between Bin and Ning, broke their line, and captured their leader.

sentences.zh: 河南賊馬進忠、馬光玉驅宛、洛之眾，箕張而西。

translations.literal: Henan rebels Ma Jinzhong and Ma Guangyu drove the masses of Wan and Luo westward like an opening fan.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan rebels Ma Jinzhong and Ma Guangyu swept the hosts of Nanyang and Luoyang westward in a spreading advance.

sentences.zh: 傳庭擊之，賊還走。

translations.literal: Chuanting attacked them and the rebels turned back and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting struck them and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 又設伏於潼關原，變蛟逐賊入伏。

translations.literal: He also set an ambush on the Tongguan plain; Bian Jiao drove the rebels into the ambush.
translations.idiomatic: He laid another ambush on the Tongguan plain, and Bian Jiao herded the rebels straight into it.

sentences.zh: 而闖王李自成者，為洪承疇所逐，盡亡其卒，以十八騎潰圍遁。

translations.literal: As for the Dashing King Li Zicheng, pursued by Hong Chengchou, he lost all his troops and escaped the broken siege with eighteen riders.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng, the Dashing King, had been hunted by Hong Chengchou until his army was destroyed; he broke out of encirclement with only eighteen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 關中群盜悉平，是為崇禎之十一年春也。

translations.literal: All the bandits of Guanzhong were completely pacified—this was the spring of the eleventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Every rebel band in Guanzhong had been crushed—this was the spring of Chongzhen's eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，大喜，先敘澄城之捷，命加傳庭部銜。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, [the emperor] was greatly pleased; he first recorded the victory at Chengcheng and ordered that Chuanting be given a ministry title.
translations.idiomatic: When word of victory reached the court, the emperor was overjoyed. He first recorded the triumph at Chengcheng and ordered that Chuanting be granted a ministry title.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌仍格不奏。

translations.literal: Sichang again blocked it and would not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang again blocked the recommendation and refused to submit it.

sentences.zh: 當是時，總理熊文燦主撫。

translations.literal: At that time Coordinator Xiong Wencan favored pacification.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the overall coordinator Xiong Wencan was committed to negotiating surrender.

sentences.zh: 湖廣賊張獻忠已降，惟河南賊如故。

translations.literal: Huguang rebel Zhang Xianzhong had already surrendered; only the Henan rebels remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong of Huguang had already submitted, but the Henan rebels were as active as ever.

sentences.zh: 羅汝才、馬進忠、賀一龍、左金王等十三部西窺潼關，聯營數十里。

translations.literal: Luo Rucai, Ma Jinzhong, He Yilong, Zuo Jinwang, and thirteen other factions eyed Tong Pass from the west, their linked camps stretching for dozens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rucai, Ma Jinzhong, He Yilong, Zuo Jinwang, and thirteen other bands watched Tong Pass from the west, their camps strung out for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 傳庭計曰：「天下大寇盡在此矣。

translations.literal: Chuanting planned, saying: "All the great bandits under Heaven are gathered here.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting reckoned: "Every major rebel in the empire is here.

sentences.zh: 我出擊其西，總理擊其東，賊不降則滅。

translations.literal: I go out and strike their west, the coordinator strikes their east—if the rebels do not surrender, then destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: If I strike from the west and the coordinator from the east, they must either surrender or be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 此賊平，天下無賊矣。

translations.literal: When these rebels are pacified, under Heaven there will be no rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Crush this force and the rebellion is finished.

sentences.zh: 獻忠即狙伏，無能為也。

translations.literal: Xianzhong, even if he lurks in ambush, can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Xianzhong is lying in wait somewhere, he can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 」乃遂引兵東，大敗賊閿鄉、靈寶山間，貫其營而東，復自東以西。

translations.literal: " He then led troops east, crushing the rebels between Wenxiang and Lingbao, piercing their camps eastward and again from east to west.
translations.idiomatic: With that he marched east, routed the rebels in the hills between Wenxiang and Lingbao, drove straight through their camps from west to east, then swept back from east to west.

sentences.zh: 賊窘甚，以文燦招降手諭上，言旦夕且降。

translations.literal: The rebels were in dire straits; they held up Wencan's handwritten order to negotiate surrender, saying they would surrender within days.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, the rebels waved Wencan's handwritten summons to surrender and claimed they would submit at any moment.

sentences.zh: 傳庭曰：「爾曹日就熊公言撫，而日攻堡屠寨不已，是偽也。

translations.literal: Chuanting said: "You people daily go to Lord Xiong to speak of pacification, yet daily attack forts and slaughter stockades without cease—this is falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting replied: "Day after day you go to Lord Xiong to talk of surrender, yet day after day you storm forts and massacre stockades—this is a sham.

sentences.zh: 降即解甲來，有說即非真降，吾明日進兵矣。

translations.literal: If you surrender, lay down your armor and come; if there is talk, it is not a true surrender—I advance troops tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to surrender, lay down your arms and come in; if there is only talk, it is not a real surrender—I march tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」明日擐甲而出，得文燦檄於途中曰：「毋妒吾撫功。

translations.literal: " The next day he donned armor and marched out; on the road he received Wencan's dispatch saying: "Do not be jealous of my pacification achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he armored up and marched out, but on the road received a dispatch from Wencan: "Do not begrudge me my success in winning them over.

sentences.zh: 」又進，得本兵嗣昌手書，亦雲。

translations.literal: " Proceeding further, he received a personal letter from War Minister Sichang saying the same.
translations.idiomatic: Farther on he received a personal letter from War Minister Sichang saying the same thing.

sentences.zh: 傳庭怏怏撤兵還。

translations.literal: Chuanting, resentful, withdrew the troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting withdrew his army in bitter frustration.

sentences.zh: 然賊迄不就撫，移瞰商、雒。

translations.literal: Yet the rebels to the end did not accept pacification and shifted to overlook Shang and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels never submitted, however, and turned their gaze toward Shangzhou and Luonan.

sentences.zh: 文燦悔，期傳庭夾擊。

translations.literal: Wencan regretted it and set a rendezvous with Chuanting for a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan repented of his policy and arranged a joint strike with Chuanting.

sentences.zh: 屬吏王文清等三戰三敗之，賊奔內鄉、淅川而去。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials Wang Wenqing and others fought three battles and defeated them three times; the rebels fled toward Neixiang and Xichuan and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenqing and other subordinates fought them three times and won three times, driving the rebels off toward Neixiang and Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 傳庭既屢建大功，其將校數奉旨優敘，嗣昌務抑之不為奏。

translations.literal: Since Chuanting had repeatedly achieved great merit, his officers and commanders several times received edicts for preferential recognition, yet Sichang deliberately suppressed them and would not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting had won victory after victory, and his officers repeatedly earned imperial orders for special commendation—but Sichang deliberately blocked every recommendation.

sentences.zh: 傳庭懇請上其籍於部，嗣昌曰：「需之。」

translations.literal: Chuanting earnestly requested that the roster be submitted to the ministry; Sichang said: "Wait for it."
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting pleaded that the roster be forwarded to the ministry. Sichang replied: "In due time."

sentences.zh: 十月，京師戒嚴，召傳庭及承疇入衛，擢兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，代總督盧象升督諸鎮援軍，賜劍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the capital was placed under martial alert; Chuanting and Chengchou were summoned to defend the capital. [Chuanting] was promoted to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War and concurrent vice censor-in-chief of the right, replacing Governor Lu Xiangsheng to command the relief armies of the various garrisons, and was granted the sword of authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, with the capital under martial law, Chuanting and Chengchou were called in to defend it. Chuanting was promoted to vice minister of War and vice censor-in-chief of the right, replacing Governor Lu Xiangsheng as commander of the relief armies from the border garrisons, and was granted the imperial sword.

sentences.zh: 當是時，傳庭提兵抵近郊，與嗣昌不協，又與中官高起潛忤，降旨切責，不得朝京師。

translations.literal: At that time Chuanting led troops to the near suburbs; he was at odds with Sichang and also clashed with eunuch Gao Qiqian; an edict descended sharply rebuking him, and he was not permitted to attend court in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chuanting had brought his army to the capital's outskirts. He was at odds with Sichang and had quarreled with the eunuch Gao Qiqian; the emperor sent down a stern rebuke and forbade him to enter the capital for an audience.

sentences.zh: 承疇至，郊勞，且命陛見，傳庭不能無觖望。

translations.literal: When Chengchou arrived, [the court] welcomed him in the suburbs and moreover ordered him to audience; Chuanting could not but feel resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengchou arrived he was welcomed in the suburbs and granted an imperial audience—Chuanting could hardly suppress his bitterness.

sentences.zh: 無何，嗣昌用承疇以為薊督，欲盡留秦兵之入援者守薊、遼。

translations.literal: Before long Sichang employed Chengchou as Ji governor and wished to retain all the Qin troops that had come in relief to garrison Ji and Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sichang installed Chengchou as governor of Ji and proposed keeping every Shaanxi unit that had marched east to garrison Ji and Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 傳庭曰：「秦軍不可留也。

translations.literal: Chuanting said: "The Qin army cannot be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting objected: "The Shaanxi troops must not be kept here.

sentences.zh: 留則賊勢張，無益於邊，是代賊撤兵也。

translations.literal: If retained, rebel strength will expand—no benefit to the border; this is withdrawing troops on the rebels' behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Keep them here and the rebels grow stronger while the frontier gains nothing—you would be pulling troops away for the enemy's benefit.

sentences.zh: 秦軍妻子俱在秦，兵日殺賊以為利，久留於邊，非嘩則逃，不復為吾用，必為賊用，是驅民使從賊也。

translations.literal: The wives and children of the Qin army are all in Qin; the troops daily kill rebels for profit. Long retained at the border, they will either mutiny or flee, no longer serving us—they will surely serve the rebels; this is driving the people to follow the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Their families are all back in Shaanxi; these men fight rebels because there is profit in it. Keep them on the frontier too long and they will riot or desert—they will no longer serve us, but the rebels—and you will be driving your own soldiers into the enemy's ranks.

sentences.zh: 安危之機，不可不察也。

translations.literal: The pivot of safety and danger—this cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the realm hangs on such decisions—you cannot afford to ignore them.

sentences.zh: 」嗣昌不聽。

translations.literal: " Sichang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 傳庭爭之不能得，不勝郁郁，耳遂聾。

translations.literal: Chuanting argued but could not prevail; overcome with gloom, his ears then went deaf.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting argued in vain; crushed by frustration, he lost his hearing.

sentences.zh: 傳庭初受命，疏言：「年來疆事決裂，由計畫差謬。

translations.literal: When Chuanting first received his commission, he memorialized, saying: "In recent years frontier affairs have ruptured because planning has been gravely mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuanting first took up his appointment, he wrote: "The frontier has collapsed in recent years because the strategy has been fundamentally wrong.

sentences.zh: 事竣，當面請決大計。

translations.literal: When affairs are concluded, I shall in person request a decision on the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: When this campaign is over, I beg to lay the grand strategy before Your Majesty in person.

sentences.zh: 」明年，帝移傳庭總督保定、山東、河南軍務。

translations.literal: " The next year the emperor transferred Chuanting to govern the military affairs of Baoding, Shandong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor reassigned Chuanting to overall command of military affairs in Baoding, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 既解嚴，疏請陛見。

translations.literal: After martial alert was lifted, he memorialized requesting an imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emergency was lifted, he submitted a memorial requesting an audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌大驚，謂傳庭將傾之，斥來役賫疏還之傳庭。

translations.literal: Sichang was greatly alarmed, saying Chuanting would bring him down; he drove back the messenger bearing the memorial and returned it to Chuanting.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang was terrified, convinced Chuanting meant to destroy him, and sent the messenger back with the memorial undelivered.

sentences.zh: 傳庭慍，引疾乞休。

translations.literal: Chuanting, indignant, cited illness and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Chuanting pleaded illness and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌又劾其托疾，非真聾，帝遂發怒，斥為民，下巡撫楊一俊核真偽，一俊奏言：「真聾，非托疾。

translations.literal: Sichang again impeached him for feigning illness, saying he was not truly deaf; the emperor then grew angry, dismissed him to commoner status, and sent him to Governor Yang Yijun to verify truth or falsehood. Yijun memorialized, saying: "Truly deaf, not feigning illness.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang then accused him of faking his deafness. The emperor flew into a rage, stripped Chuanting of office and rank, and ordered Governor Yang Yijun to investigate. Yijun reported: "He is genuinely deaf, not feigning illness.

sentences.zh: 」並下一俊獄。

translations.literal: " [The emperor] also sent Yijun to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yijun was thrown into prison as well.

sentences.zh: 傳庭長系待決，舉朝知其冤，莫為言。

translations.literal: Chuanting was long imprisoned awaiting judgment; the whole court knew his injustice, yet none spoke for him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting languished in prison awaiting sentence. The whole court knew he had been wronged, but no one dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 在獄三年，文燦、嗣昌相繼敗。

translations.literal: Imprisoned three years, Wencan and Sichang in succession met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in prison, Wencan and Sichang both suffered ruin in turn.

sentences.zh: 而是時，闖王李自成者，已攻破河南矣，犯開封，執宗龍，殺唐王，兵散而賊益橫。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the Dashing King Li Zicheng had already broken through Henan, invaded Kaifeng, captured Zonglong, killed the Prince of Tang, and with armies scattered the rebels grew all the more rampant.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Zicheng, the Dashing King, had overrun Henan, besieged Kaifeng, captured Fu Zonglong, killed the Prince of Tang, and with imperial armies in disarray the rebels grew bolder than ever.

sentences.zh: 帝思傳庭言，朝士薦者益眾。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled Chuanting's words; court officials recommending him grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered Chuanting's warnings, and ever more officials at court began recommending his recall.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，起傳庭兵部右侍郎，親御文華殿問剿賊安民之策，傳庭侃侃言。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year Chuanting was restored as vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War; the emperor personally attended at the Wenhua Hall to ask the strategy for suppressing rebels and pacifying the people, and Chuanting spoke forthrightly at length.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year Chuanting was restored to vice minister of War. The emperor received him personally in the Wenhua Hall to ask how rebels might be crushed and the people secured, and Chuanting answered with calm, confident clarity.

sentences.zh: 帝嗟嘆久之，燕勞賞賚甚渥，命將禁旅援開封。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in admiration for a long time, feasted and rewarded him very generously, and ordered him to lead the capital guard to relieve Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed with admiration, entertained him lavishly, heaped rewards upon him, and ordered him to lead the capital garrison to relieve Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 開封圍已解，賊殺陜督汪喬年，帝即命傳庭往代。

translations.literal: The siege of Kaifeng had already been lifted; the rebels killed Shaanxi Governor Wang Qiaonian, and the emperor immediately ordered Chuanting to go and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the siege of Kaifeng was lifted, the rebels had killed Shaanxi Governor Wang Qiaonian, and the emperor immediately sent Chuanting to take his place.

sentences.zh: 大集諸將於關中，縛援剿總兵賀人龍，坐之麾下，數而斬之。

translations.literal: He greatly assembled the generals in Guanzhong, bound relief-and-suppression commander He Renlong, seated him before the ranks, enumerated his crimes, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned every general in Guanzhong, bound the relief commander He Renlong, placed him before the assembled officers, recited his crimes, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 謂其開縣噪歸，猛帥以孤軍失利而獻、曹出柙也；

translations.literal: He charged that at Kaixian [Renlong] mutinied and returned, fierce commanders with isolated forces suffered defeat, and Xian and Cao came out of the cage;
translations.idiomatic: He accused Renlong of mutinying at Kaixian and marching home, of letting fierce commanders lose battles with isolated forces, and of allowing Zhang and Cao to break loose like beasts from a cage;

sentences.zh: 又謂其遇敵先潰，新蔡、襄城連喪二督也。

translations.literal: He further charged that encountering the enemy he fled first, and at Xincai and Xiangcheng two governors in succession were lost.
translations.idiomatic: he further charged that Renlong had been first to flee in every engagement, costing the empire two governors in succession at Xincai and Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 諸將莫不灑然動色者。

translations.literal: None of the generals failed to be moved and change countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer in the hall visibly paled.

sentences.zh: 傳庭既已誅殺人龍，威詟三邊，日夜治軍為平賊計，而賊遂已再圍開封。

translations.literal: Chuanting, having already executed Renlong, awed the three frontiers, day and night drilling the army to plan pacification of the rebels—yet the rebels had already besieged Kaifeng again.
translations.idiomatic: With Renlong dead, Chuanting's authority over the three frontiers was absolute; he drilled his army day and night to crush the rebels—yet even as he did so, the rebels were besieging Kaifeng again.

sentences.zh: 詔御史蘇京監延、寧、甘、固軍，趣傳庭出關。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Censor Su Jing to supervise the armies of Yan, Ning, Gan, and Gu, and urged Chuanting to exit the pass.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Censor Su Jing to oversee the Yan, Ning, Gan, and Gu garrisons and ordered Chuanting to march out through the pass at once.

sentences.zh: 傳庭上言：「兵新募，不堪用。

translations.literal: Chuanting memorialized upward, saying: "The troops are newly recruited and cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting protested: "These are raw recruits—they are not fit for battle.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 傳庭不得已出師，以九月抵潼關。

translations.literal: Chuanting, having no choice, marched out; in the ninth month he reached Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting had no choice but to take the field, reaching Tong Pass in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 大雨連旬，自成決馬家口河灌開封。

translations.literal: Heavy rain continued for ten days; Zicheng breached the Majiakou River to flood Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell for weeks on end while Zicheng broke the Majiakou dikes and flooded Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 開封已陷，傳庭趨南陽，自成西行逆秦師。

translations.literal: Kaifeng had already fallen; Chuanting hastened toward Nanyang, and Zicheng marched west to meet the Qin army.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng had already fallen. Chuanting pushed toward Nanyang while Zicheng marched west to intercept the Shaanxi army.

sentences.zh: 傳庭設三覆以待賊：牛成虎將前軍，左勷將左，鄭嘉棟將右，高傑將中軍。

translations.literal: Chuanting set three ambushes to await the rebels: Niu Chenghu commanded the vanguard, Zuo Rang the left, Zheng Jiadong the right, and Gao Jie the center army.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting laid three ambushes to trap the rebels: Niu Chenghu led the vanguard, Zuo Rang the left wing, Zheng Jiadong the right, and Gao Jie the center.

sentences.zh: 成虎陽北以誘賊，賊奔入伏中，成虎還兵而鬥，高傑、董學禮突起翼之，左勷、鄭嘉棟左右橫擊之。

translations.literal: Chenghu feigned retreat north to lure the rebels; the rebels rushed into the ambush, Chenghu turned the army back to fight, Gao Jie and Dong Xueli suddenly rose to flank them, and Zuo Rang and Zheng Jiadong struck from left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghu feigned a northward retreat to draw the rebels in; when they charged into the trap he wheeled about to fight, Gao Jie and Dong Xueli surged up on the flanks, and Zuo Rang and Zheng Jiadong struck from both sides.

sentences.zh: 賊潰東走，斬首千余。

translations.literal: The rebels broke and fled east; more than a thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fled eastward; more than a thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 追三十里，及之郟縣之冢頭，賊棄甲仗軍資於道，秦兵趨利。

translations.literal: Pursuing thirty li, they caught up at Zhongtou in Jia County; the rebels abandoned armor, weapons, and military supplies on the road, and the Qin troops rushed for profit.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran thirty li to Zhongtou in Jia County, where the rebels abandoned arms and supplies along the road and the Shaanxi troops broke ranks to seize the loot.

sentences.zh: 賊覘我軍囂，反兵乘之，左勷、蕭慎鼎之師潰，諸軍皆潰。

translations.literal: The rebels observed our army's disorder and turned their troops to strike; the armies of Zuo Rang and Xiao Shending collapsed, and all armies collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw the disorder in our ranks, wheeled about, and counterattacked; the divisions of Zuo Rang and Xiao Shending broke, and the whole army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 副將孫枝秀躍馬以追賊，擊殺數十騎，賊兵圍之，馳突不得出，馬蹶被執，植立不撓。

translations.literal: Vice general Sun Zhixiu leaped on his horse to pursue the rebels, struck and killed several dozen riders; rebel troops surrounded him, and though he charged and thrust he could not break out; his horse stumbled and he was captured, standing upright without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Vice general Sun Zhixiu spurred after the fleeing rebels and cut down dozens of horsemen before rebel troops surrounded him. He charged back and forth but could not break free; his horse fell and he was taken, yet he stood upright and unbowed.

sentences.zh: 以刃臨之，瞠目不答。

translations.literal: When blades were placed against him, he stared wide-eyed and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: They put blades to his throat; he stared back and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 一人曰：「此孫副將也。

translations.literal: One man said: "This is Vice General Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "This is Vice General Sun.

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: " They then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 參將黑尚仁亦被執不屈而見殺，覆軍數千，材官小將之歿者，張渼奎、李棲鳳、任光裕、戴友仁以下七十有八人。

translations.literal: Regimental commander Hei Shangren was also captured, would not submit, and was killed; several thousand troops were overrun; among officers and junior commanders who perished, from Zhang Meikui, Li Qifeng, Ren Guangyu, and Dai Youren downward there were seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental commander Hei Shangren was likewise captured, refused to yield, and was executed. Several thousand troops were lost, and among the officers and junior commanders who died were Zhang Meikui, Li Qifeng, Ren Guangyu, Dai Youren, and seventy-four others.

sentences.zh: 賊倍獲其所喪馬。

translations.literal: The rebels doubly recovered the horses they had lost.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels recovered twice as many horses as they had lost.

sentences.zh: 傳庭走鞏，由孟入關，執斬慎鼎；

translations.literal: Chuanting fled to Gong, entered the pass by way of Meng, and arrested and executed Shending;
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting fled to Gong County, re-entered the pass through Mengjin, and had Shending arrested and executed;

sentences.zh: 罰勷馬以二千，以勷父光先故，貸勷。

translations.literal: He fined Rang two thousand horses; because of Rang's father Guangxian, he pardoned Rang.
translations.idiomatic: He fined Zuo Rang two thousand horses in compensation, but because of Zuo Rang's father Zuoguang Xian, he spared Zuo Rang himself.

sentences.zh: 是役也，天大雨，糧不至，士卒采青柿以食，凍且餒，故大敗。

translations.literal: In this campaign heaven sent heavy rain, grain did not arrive, soldiers gathered green persimmons for food, were cold and hungry, and therefore suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That battle was lost to rain and supply failure: with no grain coming up, the troops subsisted on wild persimmons, freezing and starving until the army collapsed entirely.

sentences.zh: 豫人所謂「柿園之役」也。

translations.literal: This is what the people of Yu call "the Battle of the Persimmon Grove."
translations.idiomatic: It became known in Henan as the Battle of the Persimmon Grove.

sentences.zh: 傳庭既已敗歸陜西，計守潼關，扼京師上遊。

translations.literal: Chuanting, having been defeated and returned to Shaanxi, planned to hold Tong Pass and choke off the upper reaches above the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Chuanting withdrew to Shaanxi and set his mind on holding Tong Pass—the gateway upstream of the capital.

sentences.zh: 且我軍新集，不利速戰，乃益募勇士，開屯田，繕器，積粟，三家出壯丁一。

translations.literal: Moreover our army was newly assembled and ill suited to rapid battle; he therefore further recruited brave warriors, opened garrison fields, repaired weapons, stored grain, and levied one able-bodied man from every three households.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were freshly recruited and unfit for a quick fight, so he stepped up recruitment, opened military farms, repaired arms, stockpiled grain, and pressed one able-bodied man from every three households.

sentences.zh: 火車載火炮甲仗者三萬輛，戰則驅之拒馬，止則環以自衛。

translations.literal: There were thirty thousand flame carts bearing cannon, armor, and weapons; in battle they were driven forward to block cavalry, and at rest they were ranged in a circle for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: He fielded thirty thousand gun-carts loaded with cannon, armor, and arms—deployed as mobile barricades in action and formed into defensive rings when halted.

sentences.zh: 督工苛急，夜以繼日，秦民不能堪。

translations.literal: Supervision of labor was harsh and urgent, day following night without pause, and the people of Qin could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Construction was driven relentlessly around the clock, and the people of Shaanxi could bear it no longer.

sentences.zh: 而關中頻歲饑，駐大軍餉乏，士大夫厭苦傳庭所為，用法嚴，不樂其在秦。

translations.literal: Yet Guanzhong had suffered famine year after year; provisioning a large army was deficient; gentry and officials were weary and distressed by Chuanting's conduct—his application of law was severe—and were displeased that he remained in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong had been famine-stricken for years, and feeding a large garrison was impossible. Officials resented Chuanting's harsh methods and wished him gone from the province.

sentences.zh: 相與嘩於朝曰：「秦督玩寇矣。

translations.literal: Together they clamored at court, saying: "The governor of Qin is toying with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Officials raised an uproar at court: "The Shaanxi governor is coddling the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」又相與危語恫脅之曰：「秦督不出關，收者至矣。

translations.literal: " Together again they spoke alarming words to intimidate him, saying: "If the governor of Qin does not exit the pass, those sent to take him will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: " They piled on with threats: "If he does not march out, the arresting officers will be here.

sentences.zh: 」明年五月，命兼督河南、四川軍務，尋進兵部尚書，改稱督師，加督山西、湖廣、貴州及江南、北軍務，賜劍。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the following year he was ordered additionally to supervise military affairs in Henan and Sichuan; soon he was promoted to minister of war, his title changed to supreme commander, with added supervision of military affairs in Shanxi, Huguang, Guizhou, and the two capitals region north and south, and was granted the sword of authority.
translations.idiomatic: " The following May he was given joint command over Henan and Sichuan, soon promoted to Minister of War and styled Supreme Commander, with authority extended to Shanxi, Huguang, Guizhou, and both capitals regions—and awarded the ceremonial sword.

sentences.zh: 趣戰益急。

translations.literal: The urging to battle grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Pressure to fight mounted daily.

sentences.zh: 傳庭頓足嘆曰：「奈何乎！

translations.literal: Chuanting stamped his foot and sighed, saying: "What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting stamped his foot and cried out: "What can I do!

sentences.zh: 吾固知往而不返也。

translations.literal: I have long known that if I go I shall not return.
translations.idiomatic: I always knew this march would be one-way.

sentences.zh: 然大丈夫豈能再對獄吏乎！

translations.literal: Yet can a true man face prison officers again!
translations.idiomatic: But what man of honor could endure the prison warders a second time!

sentences.zh: 」頃之，不得已遂再議出師。

translations.literal: " Before long, having no choice, he again deliberated on marching out.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after, with no alternative, he once more resolved to take the field.

sentences.zh: 總兵牛成虎將前鋒，高傑將中軍，王定、官撫民將延、寧兵為後勁，白廣恩統火車營，檄左良玉赴汝寧夾擊。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Niu Chenghu commanded the vanguard, Gao Jie the center army, Wang Ding and Guan Fumin the Yan and Ning troops as rear strength, Bai Guang'en commanded the flame-cart camp, and a dispatch ordered Zuo Liangyu to come to Runing for a converging attack.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Chenghu led the vanguard, Gao Jie the center, Wang Ding and Guan Fumin the Yan and Ning contingents in the rear, Bai Guang'en the gun-cart corps, with orders for Zuo Liangyu to rendezvous at Runing for a pincer strike.

sentences.zh: 當是時，自成已據有河南、湖北十余郡，自號新順王，設官置戍，營襄陽而居之。

translations.literal: At that time Zicheng already held more than ten commanderies in Henan and Hubei; he styled himself King Xinshun, established officials and set garrisons, encamped at Xiangyang and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zicheng held a dozen prefectures across Henan and Hubei, proclaimed himself King Xinshun, installed an administration and garrisons, and made Xiangyang his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 將由內、淅窺商、雒，盡發荊、襄兵會於氾水、滎澤，伐竹結筏，人佩三葫蘆，將謀渡河。

translations.literal: He intended to spy toward Shang and Luo from Nei and Xi, mustered all Jing and Xiang troops to assemble at Fanshui and Xingze, cut bamboo to bind rafts, had each man carry three gourds, and planned to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to probe toward Shangzhou and Luoyang from the Inner and Outer Xichuan routes, concentrating Jingxiang forces at Fanshui and Xingze, lashing bamboo into rafts with three gourds apiece for flotation—preparing a river crossing.

sentences.zh: 傳庭分兵防禦。

translations.literal: Chuanting divided his forces for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting split his army to block each approach.

sentences.zh: 八月十日，傳庭出師潼關，次於閿鄉。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the eighth month Chuanting marched out from Tong Pass and halted at Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth of the eighth month Chuanting crossed Tong Pass and camped at Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，師次陜州，檄河南諸軍渡河進剿。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day the army halted at Shanzhou and dispatched orders for Henan forces to cross the river and advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first the army reached Shanzhou and called up the Henan garrisons to cross the river and join the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 九月八日，師次汝州，偽都尉四天王李養純降。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the ninth month the army halted at Ruzhou; the false commandant Four Heavenly Kings Li Yangchun surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth of the ninth month the army reached Ruzhou, where the rebel commandant "Four Heavenly Kings" Li Yangchun defected.

sentences.zh: 養純言賊虛實：諸賊老營在唐縣，偽將吏屯寶豐，自成精銳盡聚於襄城。

translations.literal: Yangchun reported the rebels' strength and weakness: the old camps of the various rebels were at Tang County, false generals and officials were stationed at Baofeng, and Zicheng's elite troops were all gathered at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yangchun laid out the rebel dispositions: veteran camps at Tang County, field officers at Baofeng, and Zicheng's best troops massed at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 遂破賊寶豐，斬偽州牧陳可新等。

translations.literal: Thereupon they broke the rebels at Baofeng and beheaded the false prefect Chen Kexin and others.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Baofeng, killing the rebel prefect Chen Kexin and others.

sentences.zh: 遂搗唐縣，破之，殺家口殆盡，賊滿營哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon they struck Tang County, broke it, killed dependents nearly to the last, and rebels throughout the camps wept.
translations.idiomatic: They then raided Tang County, slaughtering rebel families almost to a person; wailing filled every camp.

sentences.zh: 轉戰至郟縣，遂擒偽果毅將軍謝君友，斫賊坐纛，尾自成幾獲。

translations.literal: Turning to battle at Jia County, they captured the false Guoyi general Xie Junyou, cut down the rebels' command banner, pursued Zicheng's tail and nearly captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting on to Jia County, they took the rebel general Xie Junyou, brought down the rebel command standard, and chased Zicheng so close he nearly fell into their hands.

sentences.zh: 賊奔襄城，大軍遂進逼襄城。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Xiangcheng, and the great army then pressed close upon Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into Xiangcheng, and the main force closed in on the city.

sentences.zh: 賊懼謀降，自成曰：「無畏！

translations.literal: The rebels, in fear, plotted surrender; Zicheng said: "Do not fear!
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread and some rebels talked of surrender; Zicheng said: "Have no fear!

sentences.zh: 我殺王焚陵，罪大矣，姑決一死戰。

translations.literal: I killed princes and burned the tombs—my crime is great; for the moment let us resolve on a battle to the death.
translations.idiomatic: I killed a prince and burned the imperial tombs—our guilt is beyond pardon. Better to stake everything on one final fight.

sentences.zh: 不勝，則殺我而降未晚也。

translations.literal: If we do not win, then kill me and surrender—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we lose, execute me and surrender then—it will still be in time.

sentences.zh: 」而大軍時皆露宿與賊持，久雨道濘，糧車不能前。

translations.literal: " Yet the great army at that time all slept in the open and held against the rebels; long rain made the roads muddy, and grain carts could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: " Meanwhile the imperial army camped in the open, locked in stalemate with the enemy; weeks of rain churned the roads to mud and supply wagons could not get through.

sentences.zh: 士饑，攻郟破之，獲馬騾啖之立盡。

translations.literal: The soldiers were hungry; they attacked Jia, broke it, obtained horses and mules and ate them, devouring them instantly.
translations.idiomatic: Starving, the men stormed Jia, seized every horse and mule in the town, and devoured the meat on the spot.

sentences.zh: 雨七日夜不止，後軍嘩於汝州。

translations.literal: Rain fell seven days and seven nights without stopping; the rear army mutinied at Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell without pause for seven days and nights; the rear echelon erupted in mutiny at Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，流言四起。

translations.literal: The rebels arrived in great force, and rumors spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements poured in, and rumors flew in every direction.

sentences.zh: 不得已還軍迎糧，留陳永福為後拒。

translations.literal: Having no choice, he turned the army back to meet the grain, leaving Chen Yongfu as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: With no alternative he pulled back to meet the supply train, leaving Chen Yongfu to cover the retreat.

sentences.zh: 前軍既移，後軍亂，永福斬之不能止。

translations.literal: Once the vanguard had moved, the rear army fell into disorder; Yongfu executed men but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: As the vanguard withdrew the rear dissolved into chaos; even executions by Chen Yongfu could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 賊追及之南陽，官軍還戰。

translations.literal: The rebels pursued and caught up at Nanyang; the official army turned back to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels caught the army at Nanyang, and the government troops turned to give battle.

sentences.zh: 賊陣五重，饑民處外，次步卒，次馬軍，又次驍騎，老營家口處內。

translations.literal: The rebel formation had five layers: starving civilians on the outside, then foot soldiers, then cavalry, then again elite horsemen, with old-camp dependents on the inside.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels deployed in five rings: starving peasants outermost, then infantry, then cavalry, then crack horsemen, with veteran families and dependents at the core.

sentences.zh: 戰破其三重。

translations.literal: In battle three layers were broken.
translations.idiomatic: Battle broke through three of the five lines.

sentences.zh: 賊驍騎殊死鬥，我師陣稍動，廣恩軍將火車者呼曰：「師敗矣！

translations.literal: The rebels' elite horsemen fought to the death; our army's formation shifted slightly; an officer of Guang'en's army in charge of flame carts cried: "The army is defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Rebel shock cavalry fought with desperate fury; the government line wavered, and an officer commanding Bai Guang'en's gun-carts shouted: "The army is defeated!

sentences.zh: 」脫挽輅而奔，車傾塞道，馬掛於衡不得前，賊之鐵騎淩而騰之，步賊手白棓遮擊，中者首兜鍪俱碎。

translations.literal: " They cast off the shafts of the carts and fled; carts overturned and blocked the road, horses caught on the yoke-bars and could not advance, the rebels' iron cavalry leaped over them, foot rebels with white clubs blocked and struck—those hit had heads and helmets both shattered.
translations.idiomatic: " Gunners cut loose their traces and ran; overturned carts choked the road, horses tangled in the harness and could not move, rebel iron cavalry vaulted over the wreckage, and infantry with white clubs struck down anyone they reached—helmets and skulls alike were smashed.

sentences.zh: 自成空壁躡我，一日夜，官兵狂奔四百里，至於孟津，死者四萬余，失亡兵器輜重數十萬。

translations.literal: Zicheng emptied his ramparts and pursued us; in one day and one night the officers and soldiers ran wildly four hundred li, reaching Mengjin; more than forty thousand died, and weapons and baggage lost numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng stripped his defenses to pursue; in a single day and night the routed army ran four hundred li to Mengjin. More than forty thousand were killed, and countless arms and supplies were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 傳庭單騎渡垣曲，由閿鄉濟。

translations.literal: Chuanting alone on horseback crossed at Yuanqu and forded by way of Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting crossed alone at Yuanqu and forded back through Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 賊獲督師坐纛，乘勝破潼關，大敗官軍。

translations.literal: The rebels captured the supreme commander's command banner; riding the victory they broke Tong Pass and greatly defeated the official army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized the commander's battle standard, rode their momentum through Tong Pass, and crushed the government forces there.

sentences.zh: 傳庭與監軍副使喬遷高躍馬大呼而歿於陣，廣恩降賊。

translations.literal: Chuanting and supervising censor vice commissioner Qiao Qian'gao leaped on horses shouting loudly and died in the formation; Guang'en surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting and supervising censor Qiao Qian'gao spurred forward shouting and fell in battle; Bai Guang'en defected to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 傳庭屍竟不可得。

translations.literal: Chuanting's corpse could ultimately not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting's body was never recovered.

sentences.zh: 傳庭死，關以內無堅城矣。

translations.literal: When Chuanting died, within the pass there were no strong cities.
translations.idiomatic: With Chuanting's death, no fortified city within the passes still stood.

sentences.zh: 初，傳庭之出師也，自分必死，顧語繼妻張夫人曰：「爾若何？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chuanting was marching out, he considered himself certain to die; turning he spoke to his successor wife Lady Zhang, saying: "What will you do?
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched, Chuanting had resigned himself to death. He turned to his wife Lady Zhang and asked: "What will become of you?

sentences.zh: 」夫人曰：「丈夫報國耳，毋憂我。

translations.literal: " The lady said: "A husband serves the state—that is all; do not worry about me.
translations.idiomatic: " She replied: "A man owes his country his life—do not trouble yourself over me.

sentences.zh: 」及西安破，張率二女三妾沈於井，揮其八歲兒世寧亟避賊去之。

translations.literal: " When Xi'an fell, Zhang led her two daughters and three concubines to drown themselves in a well, and waved her eight-year-old son Shi Ning to flee quickly and escape the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xi'an fell, Lady Zhang drowned herself in a well with her two daughters and three concubines, urging her eight-year-old son Shi Ning to flee before the rebels arrived.

sentences.zh: 兒逾墻墮民舍中，一老翁收養之。

translations.literal: The boy crossed the wall and fell into a commoner's dwelling; an old man took him in and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: The boy climbed over a wall into a neighbor's yard and was taken in by an old man.

sentences.zh: 長子世瑞聞之，重趼入秦，得夫人屍井中，面如生。

translations.literal: The eldest son Shi Rui heard of it; with heavily calloused feet he entered Qin, obtained the lady's corpse in the well, her face as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Shi Rui, upon hearing the news, walked barefoot into Shaanxi, recovered his mother's body from the well—her face still lifelike.

sentences.zh: 翁歸其弟世寧，相扶攜還。

translations.literal: The old man returned his younger brother Shi Ning; supporting each other they went back together.
translations.idiomatic: The old man restored the boy to Shi Rui; the brothers supported each other home.

sentences.zh: 道路見者，知與不知皆泣下。

translations.literal: Those who saw them on the road, whether knowing them or not, all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who saw them on the road wept, stranger and acquaintance alike.

sentences.zh: 傳庭死時，年五十有一矣。

translations.literal: When Chuanting died, his years numbered fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting was fifty-one when he died.

sentences.zh: 傳庭再出師皆以雨敗也。

translations.literal: Both times Chuanting marched out, defeat came through rain.
translations.idiomatic: Both of Chuanting's campaigns ended in defeat—and both in the rain.

sentences.zh: 或言傳庭未死者，帝疑之，故不予贈蔭。

translations.literal: Some said Chuanting had not died; the emperor doubted it, and therefore granted no posthumous honors or hereditary privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors that Chuanting was still alive made the emperor withhold posthumous honors and hereditary privileges for his family.

sentences.zh: 傳庭死而明亡矣。

translations.literal: Chuanting died—and the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: With Chuanting's death, the Ming dynasty was lost.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：流賊蔓延中原，所恃以禦賊者獨秦兵耳。

translations.literal: Praise says: Rebel bands spread across the Central Plains; what was relied upon alone to resist the rebels was the Qin army.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: as rebel armies engulfed the Central Plains, only the Shaanxi troops remained to hold them back.

sentences.zh: 傅宗龍、孫傳庭遠近相望，倚以辦賊。

translations.literal: Fu Zonglong and Sun Chuanting faced each other near and far; they were leaned upon to deal with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zonglong and Sun Chuanting stood as twin pillars of the frontier defense, upon whom all hope of crushing the rebels rested.

sentences.zh: 汪喬年、楊文嶽奮力以當賊鋒，而終於潰僨。

translations.literal: Wang Qiaonian and Yang Wenyue exerted strength to meet the rebels' spearhead, yet in the end collapsed and failed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiaonian and Yang Wenyue fought with all their strength against the rebel vanguard, yet in the end their lines broke and they perished.

sentences.zh: 此殆有天焉，非其才之不任也。

translations.literal: This perhaps had heaven's hand in it; it was not that their talent could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven itself seemed arrayed against them—it was not that they lacked the talent for the task.

sentences.zh: 傳庭敗死，賊遂入關，勢以愈熾。

translations.literal: Chuanting was defeated and died; the rebels then entered the pass, and their momentum grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuanting was killed in defeat, the rebels poured through the passes and their power grew unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 存亡之際，所系豈不重哉！

translations.literal: At the juncture of survival and extinction, what was bound up in this—was it not weighty indeed!
translations.idiomatic: At the hinge of a dynasty's survival, the stakes could scarcely have been greater.
